body.text: Rādhā-kṛṣṇārcana-dīpikā
body.translated_text: <s>Rādhā-kṛṣṇārcanadīpikā</s> (A Lamp for the Worship of <s>Rādhā</s> and <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>)

children.translated_text: He whose [elder brother] is equal to <s>Sanātana</s>,
Whose elder is the glorious <s>Sanātana</s>,
Whose younger brother is <s>Śrī Vallabha</s> —
That <s>Śrī Rūpa</s> is the true refuge of <s>Jīva</s>. (1)

body.text: *NOTE: This verse is used by Jiva as the maṅgalācaraṇa in other works also.
body.translated_text: *NOTE: This verse is used by <s>Jīva</s> as the <s>maṅgalācaraṇa</s> (auspicious invocation) in other works also.

children.translated_text: Endowed with <s>Purāṇas</s>, <s>Saṃhitās</s>, <s>Tantras</s>,
<s>Mantras</s>, and <s>Śruti</s> (Vedic revelation),
May the scripture of the <s>Gītā</s> and <s>Bhāgavata</s>
Triumph in the abodes of <s>Vraja</s>! (2)
The worship of <s>Śrī Dāmodara</s> (Kṛṣṇa) and <s>Rādhā</s> is the proper [duty] of the residents of <s>Vraja</s>.
Its necessity [is established because] of the supremacy of the divine feminine (<s>Rādhā</s>) indeed. (3)

body.text: tatra kaścit śāstra-pramāṇakatvaṃ na manyate, taṃ pratīdaṃ brūmaḥ -
body.translated_text: If someone does not consider this to be established by scriptural authority, to such a person we say:

body.text:
lakṣmīr abhitaḥ strītamā gopyo lakṣmītamāḥ prathitāḥ |
rādhā gopītamā ced asyāḥ kā samā rāmā ||4|| iti ||
body.translated_text: <s>Lakṣmī</s> is the foremost among all women; the <s>gopīs</s> are declared the foremost among <s>Lakṣmīs</s>; if <s>Rādhā</s> is the foremost among <s>gopīs</s>, then what woman is equal to her? (4) — thus.

body.text: *NOTE: This verse is quoted at Gopāla-campū 1.25.
body.translated_text: *NOTE: This verse is quoted at <s>Gopāla-campū</s> 1.25.

body.text:
āstāṃ tāvat lakṣmī-vijetṛ-guṇa-gaṇa-gopī-gaṇa-pradhānatayā śrī-kṛṣṇa-sandarbhādau nirṇītā |
[*NOTE: Portions of RKAD have been lifted wholesale from the Sandarbhas.]
atra ca nirṇeṣyamāṇā svayaṃ bhagavataḥ śrī-kṛṣṇasya svayaṃ lakṣmī-rūpā śrī-rādhā | gopī-jana-mātra-saṃvalitaḥ sa upāsyata ity atra śāstrāṇi śṛṇu | tatrāroha-bhūmikā-krameṇa darśyate |
body.translated_text: Let that be. The primacy [of <s>Rādhā</s>] among the group of <s>gopīs</s>, who possess qualities that surpass even <s>Lakṣmī</s>, has been determined in the <s>Śrī Kṛṣṇa Sandarbha</s> and elsewhere. [*NOTE: Portions of RKAD have been lifted wholesale from the <s>Sandarbhas</s>.] And here, as will be determined, the Blessed Lord himself...

children.translated_text: Just as the worship of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>
Is indeed necessary,
So too [is the worship] of his devotees;
If not, there is an insurmountable fault. (5)

body.text: *NOTE: This verse is, but for mukundasya in the place of hi kṛṣṇasya, the same as LBhāg 2.1. The following section follows closely on LBhāg 2.
body.translated_text: *NOTE: This verse is, but for <s>mukundasya</s> in the place of <s>hi kṛṣṇasya</s>, the same as <s>Laghu-bhāgavatāmṛta</s> 2.1. The following section follows closely on <s>Laghu-bhāgavatāmṛta</s> 2.

body.text:
(end page 1)
atra śrī-kṛṣṇasya yathā gautamīya-tantre -
body.translated_text: Here, regarding <s>Śrī Kṛṣṇa</s>, as in the <s>Gautamīya Tantra</s>:

body.text:
asāre ghora-saṃsāre
sāraṃ kṛṣṇa-padārcanam |

children.translated_text: Having attained birth among humans,
With pure father and mother,
One who, being capable, does not worship —
Who is more sinful than such a person? (6)

body.translated_text:
In the essenceless, terrible <s>saṃsāra</s>,
the essence is the worship of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>'s feet.

body.text: mahābhārate -
body.translated_text: In the <s>Mahābhārata</s>:

children.translated_text: He who protects like a mother,
The creator of the creation and <s>saṃsāra</s>,
One who does not worship that Lord of gods —
Know him to be a slayer of <s>Brahman</s>. (7)

body.text: atha tadīyānāṃ yathā pādme -
body.translated_text: Now, regarding [the worship of] his devotees, as in the <s>Padma Purāṇa</s>:

children.translated_text: <s>Mārkaṇḍeya</s>, <s>Ambarīṣa</s>,
<s>Vasu</s>, <s>Vyāsa</s>, <s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s>,
<s>Puṇḍarīka</s>, <s>Bali</s>, <s>Śambhu</s>,
<s>Prahlāda</s>, <s>Vidura</s>, <s>Dhruva</s>, (8)
<s>Dālbhya</s>, <s>Parāśara</s>, <s>Bhīṣma</s>,
<s>Nārada</s> and others — by the <s>Vaiṣṇavas</s>
They should be served; having served <s>Hari</s>,
If not [these devotees also], the fault is supreme. (9)

body.text: tathā hari-bhakti-sudhodaye (16.76) -
body.translated_text: Likewise, in the <s>Haribhaktisudhodaya</s> (16.76):

children.translated_text: Those who, having worshiped <s>Govinda</s>,
Do not worship those who belong to him —
They are not fit for the grace
Of <s>Viṣṇu</s> — [they are] hypocrites. (10)

body.text: pādmottara-khaṇḍe -
body.translated_text: In the <s>Uttara-khaṇḍa</s> of the <s>Padma Purāṇa</s>:

children.translated_text: Of all forms of worship,
The worship of <s>Viṣṇu</s> is supreme;
But even higher than that, O <s>Devī</s>,
Is the worship of those who belong to him. (11)

body.text:
arcayitvā tu govindaṃ
tadīyān nārcayet tu yaḥ |
na sa bhāgavato jñeyaḥ
kevalaṃ dāmbhikaḥ smṛtaḥ ||12|| iti |
body.translated_text:
One who, having worshiped <s>Govinda</s>,
does not worship those who belong to him —
he should not be known as a <s>Bhāgavata</s>;
he is remembered merely as a hypocrite. (12) — thus.

body.text:
atra pūrvatra ca tadīya-śabdena tasya bhaktā eva ucyante | tat tv anye -
(end page 2)

children.translated_text: Two kinds of created beings exist in this world:
The divine and the demoniac indeed;
One devoted to <s>Viṣṇu</s> is divine;
The demoniac is the opposite of that. (13)

body.translated_text: Here and previously, by the word 'those who belong to him' (<s>tadīya</s>), his devotees alone are meant. But others [who are not devotees] —

body.text: iti viṣṇu-dharmāgni-purāṇādi-niyamāt | tat sṛṣṭyādi-līlā-gatatve 'pi tad-udāsīneṣv audāsīnyasya yogyatvam | tad-dveṣṭṛṣu tad-dveṣyasyaiveti ca | tathaiva darśitaṃ saptame rājasūyārambhe śrī-yudhiṣṭhirādibhiḥ śiśupālaṃ prati gāli-pradānādinā | ataḥ śrī-bhagavān apy uktaṃ - pravṛttiṃ ca nivṛttiṃ ca (Gītā 16.7) ity ārabhya -
body.translated_text: Thus, by the rule of the <s>Viṣṇudharma</s>, <s>Agni Purāṇa</s>, and others. Even though [all beings] are part of his creative and other <s>līlās</s> (divine play), indifference is appropriate toward those indifferent to him; and enmity is appropriate toward those who hate him. This has been shown in the Seventh [Canto of the <s>Bhāgavata</s>], at the beginning of the <s>Rājasūya</s>, in <s>Śrī Yudhiṣṭhira</s>'s...

children.text: tān ahaṃ dviṣataḥ krūrān saṃsāreṣu narādhamān |
children.translated_text: Those cruel ones who hate me, the lowest of men in <s>saṃsāra</s>,

children.text: kṣipāmy ajasram aśubhān āsurīṣv eva yoniṣu ||13||
children.translated_text: I hurl perpetually, the inauspicious, into demoniac wombs alone. (13)

body.text:
āsurīṃ yonim āpannā mūḍhā janmani janmani |
mām aprāpyaiva kaunteya tato yānty adhamāṃ gatim ||14|| (Gītā 16.19-20)
body.translated_text:
Entering demoniac wombs, deluded birth after birth,
not attaining me, O <s>Kaunteya</s>, they go to the lowest state. (14) (<s>Gītā</s> 16.19-20)

body.text: tathā -
body.translated_text: Likewise:

children.text: avajānanti māṃ mūḍhā mānuṣīṃ tanum āśritam |
children.translated_text: Fools disregard me when I assume a human form,
Not knowing my supreme nature as the great Lord of all beings. (15)

body.text:
moghāśā moghakarmāṇo moghajñānā vicetasaḥ |
rākṣasīm āsurīṃ caiva prakṛtiṃ mohinīṃ śritāḥ ||16|| (Gītā 9.11-12)
body.translated_text:
Of vain hopes, vain actions, and vain knowledge, senseless —
they resort to the deluding nature of <s>rākṣasas</s> and <s>asuras</s>. (16) (<s>Gītā</s> 9.11-12)

body.text: ity anena svabhaktāḥ stutāḥ |
body.translated_text: By this, his own devotees are praised:

children.text: mahātmānas tu māṃ pārtha daivīṃ prakṛtim āśritāḥ |
children.translated_text: But the great souls, O <s>Pārtha</s>, resorting to the divine nature,
Worship me with undistracted mind, knowing me as the imperishable source of all beings. (17)

body.text:
(end page 3)
satataṃ kīrtayanto māṃ yatantaś ca dṛḍhavratāḥ |
namasyantaś ca māṃ bhaktyā nityayuktā upāsate ||18|| (Gītā 9.13-14)
body.translated_text:
Always glorifying me, striving with firm vows,
prostrating before me with devotion, ever disciplined, they worship. (18) (<s>Gītā</s> 9.13-14)

body.text: ataivaikādaśe mad-bhakta-pūjābhyadhikā iti | mama pūjato 'py abhi sarvatobhāvenādhikā adhika-mat-prīti-karīty arthaḥ | tasmān mad-bhakta-pūjāvaśyakā cāntaraṅgā ceti sthite -
body.translated_text: Therefore, in the Eleventh [Canto]: 'The worship of my devotees is superior' — superior to my own worship in every way, producing greater pleasure in me — this is the meaning. Therefore, the worship of my devotees is both necessary and intimate. This being established:

body.text:
eteṣām api sarveṣāṃ
prahlādaḥ pravaro mataḥ |

children.text: *NOTE: These two lines are LBhāg 2.8, which finishes yat proktaṃ tasya māhātmyaṃ skānda-bhāgavatādiṣu.
children.translated_text: *NOTE: These two lines are <s>Laghu-bhāgavatāmṛta</s> 2.8, which finishes: 'whose greatness is declared in the <s>Skānda</s>, <s>Bhāgavata</s>, and other [Purāṇas
Among all devotees of <s>Hari</s>,
<s>Prahlāda</s> is indeed the greatest. (20)

body.translated_text: Of all these, <s>Prahlāda</s> is considered the greatest.

body.text: *NOTE: (SkandaP) LBhāg 2.9
body.translated_text: *NOTE: (<s>Skanda Purāṇa</s>) <s>Laghu-bhāgavatāmṛta</s> 2.9

body.text: saptame prahlādasyaiva hi vākyam --
body.translated_text: In the Seventh [Canto], these are indeed the words of <s>Prahlāda</s>:

children.translated_text: Where am I, born of <s>rajas</s>, O Lord, in this world dominated by <s>tamas</s>,
Born in a family of <s>asuras</s> — and where is your compassion?

children.text: na brahmaṇo na tu bhavasya na vai ramāyā
children.translated_text: Neither to <s>Brahmā</s>, nor to <s>Śiva</s>, nor indeed to <s>Ramā</s> (<s>Lakṣmī</s>)
Has that grace been bestowed — the lotus-hand placed upon my head. (<s>Bhāgavata Purāṇa</s> 7.9.26)

body.text: tatraiva śrī-nṛsiṃha-vākyam --
body.translated_text: In that same [Canto], the words of <s>Śrī Nṛsiṃha</s>:

body.text:
bhavanti puruṣā loke
mad-bhaktās tvām anuvratāḥ |
bhavān me khalu bhaktānāṃ

children.translated_text: The very exemplar. (22)
The <s>Pāṇḍavas</s> are the best of all, even more than one like <s>Prahlāda</s>;
The <s>Śrīmad Bhāgavata</s> is seen as the clear, proper authority [for this]. (23)

body.text: *NOTE: LBhāg 2.12, which begins pāṇḍavāḥ sarvataḥ śreṣṭhāḥ.
body.translated_text: *NOTE: <s>Laghu-bhāgavatāmṛta</s> 2.12, which begins '<s>Pāṇḍavāḥ sarvataḥ śreṣṭhāḥ</s>.'

body.text: tathā śrī-nārada-vākyam --
body.translated_text: Likewise, the words of <s>Śrī Nārada</s>:

children.translated_text: You in the human world are truly greatly fortunate —
Sages who purify the world come to visit [you];
In whose homes there dwells directly,
In disguise, the Supreme <s>Brahman</s> in human form. (<s>Bhāgavata Purāṇa</s> 7.10.48)

body.text: *NOTE: KṛṣṇaS 59* (p22), 82 (p33)
body.translated_text: *NOTE: <s>Kṛṣṇa Sandarbha</s> 59* (p22), 82 (p33)

body.text: (end page 4)

children.translated_text: He indeed, that <s>Brahman</s> greatly sought by [seekers of]
<s>Kaivalya</s>-<s>nirvāṇa</s>-bliss-experience,
Is your beloved, your friend, your maternal cousin,
Self-worthy-of-honor, performer of duties, and <s>Guru</s>. (<s>Bhāgavata Purāṇa</s> 7.10.49)

body.translated_text: (end page 4)

children.translated_text: He whose form has not been described in its reality
Even by <s>Śiva</s>, <s>Brahmā</s> (the Lotus-born), and others through their intellect,
Worshiped by silence, devotion, and tranquility —
May he, the Lord of the <s>Sātvatas</s>, be gracious! (<s>Bhāgavata Purāṇa</s> 7.10.50)

body.text: vyākhyātaṃ ca śrī-svāmi-caraṇaiḥ - prahlādasya bhāgyaṃ yena devo dṛṣṭaḥ | vayaṃ tu manda-bhāgyā iti viṣīdantaṃ rājānaṃ praty āha yūyam iti tribhiḥ | padya-trayasya tātparyārthas tair eva likhitaḥ | na tu prahlādasya gṛheṣu paraṃ brahma vasati | na ca tad-darśanārthaṃ munayas tad-gṛhān abhiyanti | na ca tasya mātuleyādi-rūpeṇa vartate | na ca svayam eva prasannaḥ | ato yūyam eva tato 'pi samatto 'pi bhūri-bhāgā iti bhāvaḥ || iti |
body.translated_text: And it has been explained by Śrī <s>Svāmī Caraṇa</s> (Sanātana Gosvāmī): [Nārada speaks] to the king who was despairing, [saying] '<s>Prahlāda</s>'s fortune is [great] — by which the Lord was seen; but we are of poor fortune.' He addresses [the king] with 'you' (<s>yūyam</s>) through three verses. The intended meaning of the three verses has been written by them [the commentators]...

children.translated_text: Because of their constant, very close proximity, and because of <s>Hari</s>'s greater affection,
Certain <s>Yādavas</s> are considered even greater than the <s>Pāṇḍavas</s>.

body.text: tathā śrī-daśame -
body.translated_text: Likewise, in the glorious Tenth [Canto]:

children.text: aho bhojayate yūyaṃ janma-bhājo nṝṇām iha |
children.translated_text: Ah! You are truly the blessed ones, born worthy in the human world,

children.text: yat paśyatā 'sakṛt kṛṣṇaṃ tad-darśanam api yoginām || (10.82.28)
children.translated_text: For you behold <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> repeatedly — a sight [not available] even to <s>yogins</s>. (<s>Bhāgavata Purāṇa</s> 10.82.28)

body.text: (end page 5)
body.translated_text: (end page 5)

children.translated_text: Seeing, touching, conversing on the path, talking together,
Sleeping, sitting, eating together, related by marriage and kinship —
For you who dwell upon the path of hell [i.e. in the material world],
In your homes, <s>Viṣṇu</s> himself was the cessation of heaven and liberation. (<s>Bhāgavata Purāṇa</s> 10.82.30)

body.text: tathā -
body.translated_text: Likewise:

body.text:
śayyāsanāṭanālāpa-
krīḍā-snānāśanādiṣu |
na viduḥ santam ātmānaṃ
vṛṣṇayaḥ kṛṣṇa-cetasaḥ ||30|| (BhP 10.90.46)
body.translated_text:
In sleeping, sitting, walking, conversing,
playing, bathing, eating, and the rest,
the <s>Vṛṣṇis</s>, whose minds were absorbed in <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>,
did not know him as the [Supreme] Self present [among them]. (30) (<s>Bhāgavata Purāṇa</s> 10.90.46)

body.text:
yadubhyo 'pi variṣṭho 'sau
bhagavān śrīmad-uddhavaḥ |
[*NOTE: The first two lines follow LBhāg 2.22. sarvebhyo for bhagavān.]
yādavendrasya yo mantrī

children.translated_text: His disciple, servant, beloved, and great one;
From childhood itself, toward <s>Govinda</s>,
His devotion is eternally the highest. (31)

body.translated_text:
Even among the <s>Yadus</s>, the most excellent
is the blessed <s>Śrīmad Uddhava</s>,
who was the minister of the king of <s>Yādavas</s>,

body.text: *NOTE: The last two lines are Lbhag 2.25.
body.translated_text: *NOTE: The last two lines are <s>Laghu-bhāgavatāmṛta</s> 2.25.

body.text: tathā tṛtīye -
body.translated_text: Likewise, in the Third [Canto]:

body.text:
yaḥ pañca-hāyano mātrā
prātar-āśāya yācitaḥ |
tan naicchad racayan yasya
saparyāṃ bāla-līlayā ||32|| (BhP 3.2.2)
body.translated_text: He who, at five years old, when asked by his mother for the morning meal, did not wish for it, [being absorbed in] arranging the worship of that [Lord] as a child's play. [verse 32] (<s>BhP</s> 3.2.2)

body.text: śrī-daśame ca --
body.translated_text: And in the glorious Tenth [Canto]:

children.text: vṛṣṇīnāṃ pravaro mantrī kṛṣṇasya dayitaḥ sakhā |
children.translated_text: 'The foremost among the <s>Vṛṣṇis</s>, the counselor, the dear friend of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>,
a direct disciple of <s>Bṛhaspati</s> — <s>Uddhava</s>, esteemed for his intelligence. [verse 33]

body.text:
tam āha bhagavān preṣṭhaṃ bhaktam ekāntinaṃ kvacit |
gṛhītvā pāṇinā pāṇiṃ prapannārtiharo hariḥ ||34|| (10.46.1-2)
body.translated_text: To him, the most beloved and exclusively devoted devotee, the Blessed Lord <s>Hari</s>, the remover of the suffering of those who take refuge [in him], once taking his hand in his own hand, spoke. [verse 34]' (<s>BhP</s> 10.46.1-2)

body.text: ekādaśe ca (16.24) tvaṃ tu bhāgavateṣv aham iti | na ca saṅkarṣaṇo na śrīr naivātmā ca yathā bhavān iti ca | ataiva tṛtīye svayaṃ tathaivācaritam --
body.translated_text: And in the Eleventh [Canto] (16.24): 'You are [the foremost] among my devotees.' And also: 'Neither <s>Saṅkarṣaṇa</s>, nor <s>Śrī</s> (Lakṣmī), nor even the Self is as [dear to me] as you.' For this very reason, in the Third [Canto], it was personally enacted thus:

body.text: (end page 6)
body.translated_text: [end page 6]

body.text:
noddhavo 'ṇv api man-nyūno
yad guṇair nārditaḥ prabhuḥ |
ato mad-vayunaṃ lokaṃ
grāhayann iha tiṣṭhatu ||35|| (BhP 3.4.3)
body.translated_text: '<s>Uddhava</s> is not in the slightest inferior to Me, since — O Lord — he is not afflicted by the <s>guṇas</s> (qualities of <s>sattva</s> and the like). Therefore, let him remain here, teaching the world My doctrine.' [verse 35] (<s>BhP</s> 3.4.3)

body.text: yad yasmād guṇaiḥ sattvādibhir nārdito na pīḍitaḥ guṇātītaḥ ity arthaḥ | yataḥ prabhuḥ bhakti-rasāsvāde prabhaviṣṇuḥ |
body.translated_text: 'Since' (<s>yad yasmāt</s>) 'he is not afflicted by the <s>guṇas</s> — <s>sattva</s> and the like' means he has transcended the <s>guṇas</s> — that is the meaning. 'Because he is lord' (<s>prabhu</s>) means he is capable of savoring the rasa (flavor) of <s>bhakti</s> (devotion).

body.text:
vraja-devyo varīyasya īdṛśād uddavād api |
yad āsāṃ prema-mādhuryaṃ sa eṣo 'py abhiyācate ||36|| (LBhāg 2.29)
body.translated_text: The goddesses of <s>Vraja</s> are superior even to such an <s>Uddhava</s> as this, for the sweetness of their <s>prema</s> (love) is such that even he himself implores it. [verse 36] (<s>LBhāg</s> 2.29)

body.text:
tathā hi daśame --
dṛṣṭvaivam ādi gopīnāṃ
kṛṣṇāveśātma-viklavam |
uddhavaḥ paramaḥ prītas tā
namasyann idaṃ jagau ||37|| (BhP 10.47.57)
body.translated_text: As indeed in the Tenth [Canto]: 'Having seen such [devotion] of the <s>gopīs</s> and more, [their state of being] overwhelmed and distracted by absorption in <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, <s>Uddhava</s>, supremely pleased, bowing down to them, sang this.' [verse 37] (<s>BhP</s> 10.47.57)

body.text: namasyann iti vartamāna-śatṛ-prayogo namaskārasyānavacchinnatvaṃ bodhayati | idaṃ vakṣyamāṇaṃ tad evāha --
body.translated_text: 'Bowing down' (<s>namasyan</s>) — the use of the present participle indicates the unceasing nature of the salutation. 'This' refers to what is about to be spoken — and that is what he states:

body.text:
etāḥ paraṃ tanu-bhṛto bhuvi gopa-vadhvo
govinda evam akhilātmani rūḍha-bhāvāḥ |
vāñchanti yad bhava-bhiyo munayo vayaṃ ca
kiṃ brahma-janmabhir ananta-kathā-rasasya ||38|| [BhP 10.47.58]
body.translated_text: 'These cowherd women on earth are the supreme among embodied beings, for they have developed a deeply established love (<s>bhāva</s>) for <s>Govinda</s>, who is the Self of all. That which sages who fear [the cycle of] existence, and we ourselves, desire — of what use are births as <s>Brahman</s> to one who relishes the nectar of the stories of the Infinite One?' [verse 38] [<s>BhP</s> 10.47.58]

children.text: bhāvasya durlabhatvād dhi tāsāṃ tat-siddhaye punaḥ |
children.translated_text: Because of the extreme rarity of that <s>bhāva</s> (love), in order to attain it,
even a birth as a blade of grass sprinkled by the dust of their feet is implored. [verse 39]

body.text:
*NOTE: The second line is exactly 2.41, the first line of which is
na citraṃ prema-mādhuryam
āsāṃ vāñched yad uddhavaḥ |
body.translated_text: NOTE: The second line is exactly 2.41, the first line of which is: 'It is no wonder that <s>Uddhava</s> should desire the sweetness of the <s>prema</s> (love) of these [<s>gopīs</s>

body.text: tathā hi śrī-daśame -
body.translated_text: As indeed in the glorious Tenth [Canto]:

body.text:
āsām aho caraṇa-reṇu-juṣām ahaṃ syām
vṛndāvane kim api gulma-latauṣadhīnām |
(end page 7)
yā dustyajaṃ sva-janam ārya-pathaṃ ca hitvā
bhejur mukunda-padavīṃ śrutibhir vimṛgyām ||40|| [BhP 10.47.61]
body.translated_text: 'May I become any one of the shrubs, creepers, or herbs in <s>Vṛndāvana</s> that are honored by the dust of their feet — they who abandoned what is so difficult to give up — their own people and the path of propriety — and worshiped the path of <s>Mukunda</s> (the Liberator), which is sought by the <s>śrutis</s> (scriptures).' [verse 40] [<s>BhP</s> 10.47.61]

body.text: tasyā mṛgyatvaṃ śrutibhir evoktaṃ, yathā tatraiva --
body.translated_text: That it is sought by the <s>śrutis</s> is stated by the <s>śrutis</s> themselves, as in that very [text]:

body.text:
nibhṛta-marun-manokṣa-dṛḍha-yoga-yujo hṛdi yan
munaya upāsate tad-arayo 'pi yayuḥ smaraṇāt |
striya urugendra-bhoga-bhuja-daṇḍa-viṣakta-dhiyo
vayam api te samāḥ sama-dṛśo 'ṅghri-saroja-sudhāḥ ||41|| (BhP 10.87.23)
body.translated_text: 'That which the sages, having restrained breath, mind, and senses through firm <s>yoga</s>, worship in the heart — even His enemies attained [it] through remembrance; the women (<s>gopīs</s>), their minds fixed upon the embrace of His great serpent-like arms — and we too are equal, of equal vision, [having attained] the nectar of His lotus feet.' [verse 41] (<s>BhP</s> 10.87.23)

body.text:
atra pratiyugmāntarasthasyāpi śabdasya dvayena yugma-dvayaṃ pṛthag avamyate | tataś ca tad brahmākhya tat taṃ munaya upāsate tad arayo 'pi yayuḥ smaraṇāt | striyaḥ śrī-vraja-devyaḥ aṅghri-saroja-sudhās tat-prema-maya=mādhuryāṇi yayuḥ | vayam api samadṛśas tābhiḥ sama-bhāvāḥ satyaḥ samās tābhiḥ tulyatāṃ prāptāḥ | vyūhāntareṇa gopyo bhūtvā tavāṅghri-saroja-sudhā yayima ity arthaḥ | atra bṛhad-vāmana-purāṇe tāsāṃ prārthanā pūrvakāṇi vākyāni santi | strī-śabdasya gopī vācakatvam | tad arayo 'pi yayuḥ smaraṇād ity anenāsurāṇām api mokṣa-dātṛtvena anyatayā prasiddhasya śrī-kṛṣṇasyaivālambanatvena labdhatvāt | tāsām eva tasmin kevalena rāgeṇa bhajana-prasiddheḥ | tad etad apy āstām śrī-nārāyaṇāṅga-sthitāyā lakṣmīto 'pi tāsāṃ parama-vailakṣaṇyaṃ
tenaiva tādṛśa-nija-bhakti-hetutvena darśitam | yathā tatraiva -
body.translated_text: Here, even the word standing between the two verse-pairs is separately construed with both pairs. Thus: 'That' — called <s>Brahman</s> — 'that' the sages worship; 'even His enemies attained [it] through remembrance.' The 'women' are the glorious goddesses of <s>Vraja</s>; 'the nectar of His lotus feet' — the sweetness consisting of their <s>prema</s> (love) — they attained. 'We too' — having equal vision — having the same disposition (<s>sama-bhāva</s>) as them — 'equal' means having attained equality with them. Having become <s>gopīs</s> through another emanation (<s>vyūhāntareṇa</s>), 'we attained the nectar of your lotus feet' — that is the meaning. Here, in the <s>Bṛhad-Vāmana Purāṇa</s>, there are statements that include their prior prayers. The word '<s>strī</s>' (woman) denotes <s>gopīs</s>. 'Even His enemies attained [it] through remembrance' — by this, since even <s>asuras</s> (demons) gained liberation through having <s>Śrī Kṛṣṇa</s> alone — who is otherwise famous as the granter of <s>mokṣa</s> — as their focus, and since those [<s>gopīs</s>] are famous for worshiping Him through attachment (<s>rāga</s>) alone; let this be set aside — even from <s>Lakṣmī</s>, who abides on the body of <s>Śrī Nārāyaṇa</s>, the supreme distinctness of those [<s>gopīs</s>] is shown by that very [Lord] as being due to such unique devotion. As in that very [text]:

body.text:
(end page 9)
nāyaṃ śriyo 'ṅga u nitānta-rateḥ prasādaḥ
svar-yoṣitāṃ nalina-gandha-rucāṃ kuto 'nyāḥ ||42|| (BhP 10.47.60)
body.translated_text: 'This grace is not [available to] <s>Śrī</s> (Lakṣmī), the constant companion of His bosom, nor to the women of heaven with their lotus-like fragrance and beauty — what then of others?' [verse 42] (<s>BhP</s> 10.47.60)

body.text:
ity anena lakṣmyādikā niravaśeṣā eva striyo nāmubhiḥ sālakṣaṇyaṃ prāpnuvantīti vilakṣaṇā | tatrāpy udagād ity anena sa prasādas tāsu rāsa-prasaṅge uditavān eva na tu jāta iti svābhāvika-premavatyaḥ | kevalasya śrī-vṛndāvana-vihāriṇaḥ pūrṇa-bhagavataḥ sarvato vilakṣaṇasya nitya-preyasī-rūpā iti | sarvato vilakṣaṇā-lakṣmī-viśeṣatvena prāptāḥ | tasmāt tābhiḥ saha tasya pūjanam āvaśyakam ity āyātam | tataḥ sthūṇa-nikhanana-nyāyena tad-arthaṃ tāsāṃ svarūpaṃ nirūpyate | tatrādau śrī-bhagavat-sandarbhe
[*NOTE: This is the starting point of the Bhagavat-sandarbha. The two following verses are quoted in section 16 and 21.]
brahmeti paramātmeti bhagavān iti śabdyate ity (BhP 1.2.11) ādinā śrī-bhagavantaṃ suṣṭhu nirdhārya tasya śakti-dvayī nirūpitā | māyākhyā svarūpa-bhūtākhyā ca |
body.translated_text: By this [verse], all women without exception — <s>Lakṣmī</s> and the rest — do not attain likeness with these [<s>gopīs</s>]; they are distinct. Moreover, by the word '<s>udagāt</s>' (arose), that grace arose in them during the <s>Rāsa</s>-<s>līlā</s> — it was not newly born; thus they are possessors of natural <s>prema</s> (love). [They are] the eternal beloveds of the complete <s>Bhagavān</s> (Supreme Lord), who sports solely in <s>Śrī Vṛndāvana</s> and is distinct from all [other manifestations]. Having attained [the status of] a special form of <s>Lakṣmī</s> distinct from all [others]. Therefore, it follows that worship of Him together with them is essential. Then, by the principle of 'driving in the post' (<s>sthūṇā-nikhanana-nyāya</s>), their essential nature is determined for that purpose. Therein, first, in the <s>Śrī Bhagavat-sandarbha</s>, having firmly established the Blessed Lord through [the verse beginning] 'He is called <s>Brahman</s>, <s>Paramātman</s>, and <s>Bhagavān</s>' (<s>BhP</s> 1.2.11) and so forth, His twofold power (<s>śakti</s>) is described: one called <s>Māyā</s>, and one that is essential to His own nature (<s>svarūpa-bhūtā</s>).

body.text: tatra --
body.translated_text: Therein:

children.translated_text: 'That which appears apart from [the true] reality,
and which does not appear in the Self,
that one should know as the <s>Māyā</s> (illusion) of the Self,
like a reflection and like darkness.' [<s>BhP</s> 2.9.33]

body.text: ity anena -
body.translated_text: By this, and by:

children.translated_text: 'This <s>Māyā</s> of the Blessed Lord, the cause of creation, maintenance, and dissolution,

children.text: tri-varṇā varṇitāsmābhiḥ kiṃ bhūyaḥ śrotum icchasi || (BhP 11.3.16)
children.translated_text: has been described by us as having three colors (<s>guṇas</s>) — what more do you wish to hear?' (<s>BhP</s> 11.3.16)

body.text: ity anena māyā-śaktir nirūpitā | tatra tasyā aṃśāś ca darśitāḥ ||
body.translated_text: — by this, the <s>Māyā-śakti</s> (power of illusion) is described. And therein its parts are shown.

body.text: atha yan na spṛśanti na vidur mano buddhīndriyā sarvaiḥ ity (BhP 6.16.20) ādinā |
body.translated_text: Now, through [the verse beginning] 'which neither the mind, <s>buddhi</s> (intellect), nor all the senses touch or know' (<s>BhP</s> 6.16.20) and so forth,

children.translated_text: 'You are the primordial <s>Puruṣa</s>, directly
the Lord (<s>Īśvara</s>), beyond <s>Prakṛti</s> (material nature),
having cast off <s>Māyā</s>, through the <s>Cit-śakti</s> (consciousness-power),
established in <s>kaivalya</s> (absolute oneness), in the Self.' [<s>BhP</s> 1.7.23]

body.text:
ity anena ca svarūpa-bhūtācintya-śaktir darśitā | tasyā vṛtti-bhedenāntāyāḥ --
śriyā puṣṭyā girā kāntyā kīrtyā tuṣṭyelayor jayā ity ādi kiyanto bhedāś ca darśitā (BhP 10.39.55) | sā ca śakti-dvayī aparā ceti śrī-viṣṇu-purāṇe darśitā --
body.translated_text: By this, the inconceivable power that is essential to His nature (<s>svarūpa-bhūtā acintya-śakti</s>) is shown. Through the differentiation of its function — as <s>Śrī</s>, <s>Puṣṭi</s>, <s>Girā</s>, <s>Kānti</s>, <s>Kīrti</s>, <s>Tuṣṭi</s>, <s>Ilā</s>, <s>Jaya</s> — several divisions are shown (<s>BhP</s> 10.39.55). And that twofold power is shown as '<s>aparā</s>' (lower) in the <s>Śrī Viṣṇu Purāṇa</s>:

children.translated_text: 'In all beings, O Self of all,
that power of yours which is the lower (<s>aparā</s>),
which depends on the <s>guṇas</s> — homage to that
eternal one, O Lord of the gods. [verse 45]

body.text:
yātīta-gocarā vācāṃ
manasāṃ cāviśeṣaṇā |
jñāni-jñāna-paricchedyā
vande tām īśvarīṃ parām ||46|| ity anena (ViP 1.19.76-77) ||
body.translated_text: That which is beyond the reach of words, indistinguishable by the mind, to be apprehended only by the knowledge of the knower — I salute that supreme Sovereign Lady (<s>Īśvarī</s>).' [verse 46] By this (<s>ViP</s> 1.19.76-77).

body.text: tatra prathamā śrī-vaiṣṇavānāṃ jagadvad-upekṣaṇīyā yan-mayī eva khalu tasya jagattā | dvitīyā tu teṣāṃ śrī-bhagavad-upāsyā tadīya-svarūpa-bhūtā yan-mayy eva khalu tasya bhagavattā | tatraikam eva svarūpāṃśitvena śaktimattvena ca virājatīti | yasya śakteḥ svarūpa-bhūtatvaṃ nirūpitam | cic-chakti-mattā pradhānena virājamānaṃ bhagavat-saṃjñam āpnotīti tatraiva darśitam eva | tad evaṃ śaktitva-prādhānyena virājamānāṃ lakṣmī-saṃjñām āpnotīti darśayituṃ prakaraṇam utthāpyate |
body.translated_text: Therein, the first [power, <s>Māyā</s>] is to be disregarded by the <s>Śrī Vaiṣṇavas</s> like the world, since His nature as the world is indeed constituted by that [<s>Māyā</s>]. But the second [power, <s>svarūpa-śakti</s>] is to be worshiped by them as belonging to the Blessed Lord, being essential to His own nature, since His nature as <s>Bhagavān</s> is indeed constituted by that [power]. Therein, one and the same [Lord] shines forth both as possessing a part of His essential nature (<s>svarūpāṃśitva</s>) and as possessing power (<s>śaktimatva</s>). The essential nature of that power has been described. The <s>Bhagavat</s> designation is attained by that [Lord] who shines forth primarily through the <s>Cit-śakti</s> (consciousness-power) — this has been shown in that very [<s>Sandarbha</s>]. Thus, to show that [this power], shining forth primarily through its character as <s>śakti</s>, attains the designation <s>Lakṣmī</s>, the topic is raised.

body.text: *NOTE: The following passage ending with viśuddhatvam is in BhagS 117.
body.translated_text: Therein, first: since the essential nature is one alone — consisting of being (<s>sattva</s>), consciousness (<s>citta</s>), and bliss (<s>ānanda</s>) — the essential power too, though one, is threefold. As stated in the <s>Viṣṇu Purāṇa</s>:

body.text: tatra tāvad ekasyaiv svarūpasya sattvāc cittād ānandāc ca svarūpa-bhūtā śaktir apy ekā tridhā | tad uktaṃ viṣṇu-purāṇe --

hlādinī sandhinī saṃvit
tvayy ekā sarva-saṃsthitau |
hlāda-tāpa-karī miśrā
tvayi no guṇa-varjite ||47|| iti (ViP 1.12.68)
body.translated_text: '<s>Hlādinī</s> (the bliss-giving), <s>Sandhinī</s> (the existence-giving), and <s>Saṃvit</s> (the cognition-giving) — though one in you who are the foundation of all — [become] pleasure-giving, pain-giving, and mixed in those devoid of your qualities.' [verse 47] (<s>ViP</s> 1.12.68)

body.text: vyākhyātaṃ ca svāmibhiḥ | hlādinī āhlāda-karī (end page 10) sandhinī santatā saṃvid vidyā-śaktiḥ | ekā mukhyā avyabhicāriṇī svarūpa-bhūteti yāvat | sā sarva-saṃsthitau sarvasya samyak sthitir yasmāt tasmin sarvādhiṣṭhāna-bhūte tvayy eva na tu jīveṣu ca sā guṇamayī trividhā sā tvayi nāsti | tām evāha hlāda-tāpa-karī miśrā iti | hlāda-karī manaḥ-prasādotthā sāttvikī | tāpakarī viṣaya-viyogādiṣu tāpa-karī tāmasī | tad-ubhaya-miśrā viṣaya-janyā rājasī | tatra hetuḥ -- sattvādi-guṇa-varjite | tad uktaṃ sarvajña-sūktau -
body.translated_text: And this has been explained by the master [<s>Śrīdhara Svāmī</s>]: <s>Hlādinī</s> means 'producing delight'; <s>Sandhinī</s> means 'continuous [existence]'; <s>Saṃvit</s> is the power of knowledge (<s>vidyā-śakti</s>). 'One' (<s>ekā</s>) means primary, unerring — meaning essential to His nature. 'In you who are the foundation of all' (<s>sarva-saṃsthitau</s>) — in you who are the foundation of everything, that [power] exists; but not in the individual souls (<s>jīvas</s>). That threefold [power] consisting of the <s>guṇas</s> does not exist in you. He states that very [power]: '<s>hlāda-tāpa-karī miśrā</s>' — 'pleasure-giving' is the <s>sāttvika</s> (pure) [aspect], arising from mental satisfaction; 'pain-giving,' producing pain in the separation from objects and the like, is the <s>tāmasa</s> (dark) [aspect]; 'mixed' with both of those, born of sense-objects, is the <s>rājasa</s> (passionate) [aspect]. The reason for this: 'devoid of the <s>guṇas</s> such as <s>sattva</s> and the like' [in you]. As stated in the <s>Sarvajña-sūkta</s>:

body.text:
hlādinyā saṃvid-āśliṣṭaḥ
sac-cid-ānanda īśvaraḥ |
svāvidyā-saṃvṛto jīvaḥ
saṅkleśa-nikarākaraḥ ||48|| iti (Bhāvārtha-dīpikā 1.7.6)
body.translated_text: Embraced by <s>hlādinī</s> (bliss potency) and <s>saṃvit</s> (cognitive potency), the Lord is <s>sac-cid-ānanda</s> (existence-consciousness-bliss); the <s>jīva</s> (individual soul), covered by his own <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance), is a mine of afflictions. (Verse 48) Thus (<s>Bhāvārtha-dīpikā</s> 1.7.6).

body.text: atra kramād utkarṣeṇa sandhinī-saṃvid-dhlādinyā jñeyāḥ | tatra ca sati ghaṭānāṃ ghaṭatvam iva sarveṣāṃ satāṃ vastūnāṃ pratīter nimittam iti kvacit sattā-svarūpatvena āmnāto 'py asau bhagavān sad eva somyedam agra āsīd ity atra sad-rūpatvena vyāpadiśyamānā mayā sattāṃ dadhāti dhārayati ca sā sarva-deśa-kāla-dravyādi-prāptikarī sandhinī | tathā saṃvid-rūpo 'pi yayā saṃvetti saṃvedayati ca sā saṃvit | tathā hlāda-rūpo 'pi yayā saṃvid utkaṭa-rūpayā taṃ hlādaṃ saṃvetti saṃvedayati ca sā hlādinīti vivecanīyam |
body.translated_text: Here, <s>sandhinī</s> (existential potency), <s>saṃvit</s> (cognitive potency), and <s>hlādinī</s> (bliss potency) should be understood in order of ascending excellence. Among these, just as the 'pot-ness' of pots [is their common nature], so <s>sattā</s> (existence) is the ground of the perception of all existing things. Although the Lord is sometimes spoken of as having existence as His essential nature — as in 'O <s>Saumya</s>, in the beginning this was Being alone' — the <s>sattā</s> designated as His 'Being-nature' is sustained and upheld by Me; that which brings about the attainment of all places, times, substances, etc. is <s>sandhinī</s>. Likewise, though He is also of the nature of <s>saṃvit</s> (consciousness), that by which He cognizes and causes to cognize is <s>saṃvit</s>. Similarly, though He is also of the nature of <s>hlāda</s> (bliss), that by which, in an intensified form of <s>saṃvit</s>, He experiences and causes the experience of that bliss — that is <s>hlādinī</s>. This should be carefully discerned.

body.text:
tad evaṃ tasyā mūla-śaktes try-ātmakatvena siddhe yena sva-prakāśatā-lakṣaṇena tad-vṛtti-viśeṣeṇa svarūpaṃ svayaṃ svarūpa-śaktir vā viśiṣṭam āvirbhavati tad viśuddha-sattvam | tac cānya-nirapekṣayas tat-prakāśa iti jñāpana-jñāna-vṛttikatvāt saṃvid eva | asya māyayā sparśābhāvāt viśuddhatvam |
[*NOTE: This entire section beginning with hlādinī sandhinī saṃvit is found in Bhagavat-sandarbha, section 117.]
body.translated_text: Thus, with the threefold nature of that fundamental potency established, the particular function of self-luminosity by which His essential nature, or the <s>svarūpa-śakti</s> (essential potency) itself, manifests in a distinguished way — that is <s>viśuddha-sattva</s> (pure existence). And since it is independent of anything else, its manifestation being knowledge whose function is illumination and cognition — it is <s>saṃvit</s> itself. Its purity is because it has no contact with <s>māyā</s>. [NOTE: This entire section beginning with '<s>hlādinī</s> <s>sandhinī</s> <s>saṃvit</s>' is found in <s>Bhagavat-sandarbha</s>, section 117.]

body.text: tad uktaṃ śrī-viṣṇu-purāṇe (end page 12) -
body.translated_text: This is stated in the <s>Śrī Viṣṇu Purāṇa</s> (end of page 12) —

body.text:
sattvādayo na santīśe
yatra ca prākṛtā guṇāḥ |
sa śuddhaḥ sarva-śuddhebhyaḥ
pumān ādyaḥ prasīdatu ||49|| iti | [ViP 1.9.44]
body.translated_text: <s>Sattva</s> and the other <s>prākṛta guṇas</s> (material qualities) do not exist in the Lord; He is pure, the purest of all pure beings — may that primordial <s>Puruṣa</s> be gracious! (Verse 49) [<s>ViP</s> 1.9.44]

body.text: śrī-daśame ca viśuddha-sattvaṃ tava dhāma śāntam ity ādi (BhP 10.27.4)
body.translated_text: And in the Tenth [Canto of the <s>Bhāgavata</s>]: 'Your abode is <s>viśuddha-sattva</s> (pure existence), peaceful,' etc. (<s>BhP</s> 10.27.4)

children.translated_text: <s>Hari</s> indeed is directly beyond the <s>guṇas</s> (qualities),
The <s>Puruṣa</s> transcending <s>Prakṛti</s> (primordial nature);
He is the all-seeing witness —
By worshipping Him, one becomes free from the <s>guṇas</s>. [<s>BhP</s> 10.88.5]

body.text: ekādaśe ca sattvaṃ rajas tama iti guṇā jīvasya naiva me iti [BhP 11.25.12] | gītopaniṣatsu ca -
body.translated_text: And in the Eleventh [Canto]: '<s>Sattva</s>, <s>rajas</s>, and <s>tamas</s> — these <s>guṇas</s> belong to the <s>jīva</s>, not to Me' [<s>BhP</s> 11.25.12]. And in the <s>Gītopaniṣads</s> —

children.text: ye caiva sāttvikā bhāvā rājasās tāmasāś ca ye |
children.translated_text: Those states of being that are <s>sāttvika</s> (of goodness), <s>rājasa</s> (of passion), and <s>tāmasa</s> (of ignorance) —

children.text: matta eveti tān viddhi na tv ahaṃ teṣu te mayi ||
children.translated_text: Know them to be from Me alone, yet I am not in them, nor are they in Me.

children.text: tribhir guṇa-mayair bhāvair ebhiḥ sarvam idaṃ jagat |
children.translated_text: By these three states of being composed of the <s>guṇas</s>, this entire world

children.text: mohitaṃ nābhijānāti mām ebhyaḥ param avyayam || iti [Gītā 7.12-3]
children.translated_text: Is deluded and does not recognize Me, who am beyond these and imperishable. [<s>Gītā</s> 7.12-13]

body.text:
tatra cedam eva viśuddha-sattvaṃ sandhiny-aṃśa-pradhānaṃ ced ādhāra-śaktiḥ | saṃvid-aṃśa-pradhānam ātma-vidyā | hlādinī-sārāṃśa-pradhānaṃ guhya-vidyā | yugapat śakti-traya-pradhānaṃ mūrtiḥ | atrādhāra-śaktyā bhagavad-dhāma prakāśate | tad uktaṃ - yat sātvatāḥ puruṣa-rūpam uśanti sattvaṃ loko yata [BhP 12.8.40]
[*NOTE: This appears to be evidence that 8 is the original source of the material, not 117. To be followed.]
iti |
body.translated_text: Here, this very <s>viśuddha-sattva</s>, when predominated by the <s>sandhinī</s> aspect, is the <s>ādhāra-śakti</s> (supporting potency). When predominated by the <s>saṃvit</s> aspect, it is <s>ātma-vidyā</s> (self-knowledge). When predominated by the essential aspect of <s>hlādinī</s>, it is <s>guhya-vidyā</s> (secret knowledge). When all three potencies are simultaneously predominant, it is the <s>mūrti</s> (divine form). Here, by the <s>ādhāra-śakti</s>, the Lord's <s>dhāma</s> (abode) is manifested. As stated: 'That which the <s>Sātvatas</s> recognize as the form of the <s>Puruṣa</s> — that <s>sattva</s> from which the world [arises]' [<s>BhP</s> 12.8.40]. [NOTE: This appears to be evidence that section 8 is the original source of the material, not section 117. To be followed.]

body.text: tathā jñāna-tat-pravaraka-lakṣaṇa-vṛtti-dvayakayātma-vidyayā tad-vṛtti-rūpam upāsakāśrayaṃ jñānaṃ prakāśate | evaṃ bhakti-tat-pravartaka-lakṣaṇa-vṛtti-dvayakayā guhya-vidyayā tad-vṛtti-rūpā prītyātmikā bhaktiḥ prakāśate |
body.translated_text: Likewise, by <s>ātma-vidyā</s>, which has the dual function of knowledge and its promulgation, the knowledge that is the form of that function and the basis for worshippers is manifested. Similarly, by <s>guhya-vidyā</s>, which has the dual function of <s>bhakti</s> (devotion) and its promulgation, <s>bhakti</s> whose essence is loving affection (<s>prīti</s>) and which is the form of that function, is manifested.

body.text: ete eva viṣṇu-purāṇe lakṣmī-stave spaṣṭīkṛte - (end page 12)
body.translated_text: These very [potencies] are clarified in the hymn to <s>Lakṣmī</s> in the <s>Viṣṇu Purāṇa</s> — (end of page 12)

body.text:
yajña-vidyā mahā-vidyā
guhya-vidyā ca śobhate |
ātma-vidyā ca devi tvaṃ

children.translated_text: And <s>guhya-vidyā</s> (secret knowledge) resplendent; you are <s>ātma-vidyā</s> (self-knowledge), the bestower of the fruit of liberation. [<s>ViP</s> 1.9.118]

body.translated_text: O <s>Devī</s>, you are <s>yajña-vidyā</s> (knowledge of sacrifice), <s>mahā-vidyā</s> (great knowledge),

body.text:
yajña-vidyā karma | mahā-vidyā aṣṭāṅga-yogaḥ | guhya-vidyā bhaktiḥ | ātma-vidyā jñānam | tat-tat-sarvāśrayatvāt tvam eva tat-tad-rūpā vividhānāṃ muktīnām anyeṣāṃ ca vividhānāṃ phalānāṃ dātrī bhavasīty arthaḥ |k
[*NOTE: k. This section can be found in RKAD 12-13.] śrutiś ca parāsya śaktir vividhaiva śrūyate svābhākiī jñāna-bala-kriyā ceti |
body.translated_text: <s>Yajña-vidyā</s> is ritual action (<s>karma</s>). <s>Mahā-vidyā</s> is the eightfold <s>yoga</s> (<s>aṣṭāṅga-yoga</s>). <s>Guhya-vidyā</s> is <s>bhakti</s> (devotion). <s>Ātma-vidyā</s> is <s>jñāna</s> (knowledge). Because you are the basis of all of these, you yourself, in each of those forms, are the bestower of various types of <s>mukti</s> (liberation) and other various fruits — this is the meaning. The <s>śruti</s> also [states]: 'The supreme potency of that [Lord] is heard of as manifold — His natural knowledge, strength, and action.'

body.text: athaivambhūtānanta-vṛttikā yā svarūpa-śaktiḥ sā tv iha bhagavad-vāmāṃśa-vartino mūrtimato lakṣmīr evety āha anapāyinī bhagavatī śrīḥ sākṣād ātmano hareḥ | [BhP 12.11.20] iti | ṭīkā ca - anapāyinī hareḥ śaktiḥ | tatra hetuḥ sākṣād ātmanaḥ sva-svarūpasya cid-rūpatvāt tasyās tad-abhedād ity arthaḥ ity eṣā |
body.translated_text: Now, that <s>svarūpa-śakti</s> (essential potency) which has such infinite functions — she is indeed <s>Lakṣmī</s> herself, embodied and existing in the left side of the Lord. He states: 'The inseparable, divine <s>Śrī</s> is the very self of <s>Hari</s>' [<s>BhP</s> 12.11.20]. And the commentary: 'Inseparable' — she is <s>Hari</s>'s potency. The reason for this: 'the very self' — because of the conscious nature of His own essential form, and because of her non-difference from that — this is the meaning.

body.text: atra sākṣāt-śabdena māyā paraity abhimukhe ca vilajjamānā iti [BhP 2.7.47] vimohitā vikatthante mamāham iti durdhiyaḥ | [BhP 2.5.13] ity uktvā māyā neti dhvanitam | atra anapāyitvaṃ yathā hayaśīrṣa-pañcarātre -
body.translated_text: Here, by the word 'directly' (<s>sākṣāt</s>), it is implied that [this refers] not to <s>Māyā</s>, as [indicated by]: '<s>Māyā</s> turns away and is ashamed in His presence' [<s>BhP</s> 2.7.47], and 'Those of perverted understanding, deluded [by <s>Māyā</s>], boast "mine" and "I"' [<s>BhP</s> 2.5.13] — thus it is suggested that [<s>Śrī</s>] is not <s>Māyā</s>. Her inseparability is as [stated] in the <s>Hayaśīrṣa Pañcarātra</s> —

body.text:
paramātmā harir devaḥ tac-chaktiḥ śrīr ihoditā |
śrīr devī prakṛtiḥ proktā keśavaḥ puruṣaḥ smṛtaḥ |
na viṣṇunā vinā devī na hariḥ padmajāṃ vinā ||51|| iti |
body.translated_text: The Supreme Self is Lord <s>Hari</s>; His potency, <s>Śrī</s>, is here declared. <s>Śrī Devī</s> is called <s>Prakṛti</s> (the [spiritual] nature); <s>Keśava</s> is known as <s>Puruṣa</s>. Without <s>Viṣṇu</s> there is no <s>Devī</s>, nor is <s>Hari</s> without <s>Padmajā</s> (the lotus-born one). (Verse 51)

body.text: viṣṇu-purāṇe (ViP 1.9.143) -
body.translated_text: In the <s>Viṣṇu Purāṇa</s> (<s>ViP</s> 1.9.143) —

children.text: nityaiva sā jagan-mātā viṣṇuḥ śrīr anapāyinī |
children.translated_text: She is eternal, the Mother of the world — <s>Viṣṇu</s>'s <s>Śrī</s>, inseparable.

children.text: yathā sarva-gato viṣṇus tathā śrīs tat-sahāyinī ||52||
children.translated_text: Just as <s>Viṣṇu</s> is all-pervading, so is <s>Śrī</s>, His companion. (Verse 52)

body.text: *NOTE: This section quoted from Bhagavat-sandarbha 118.
body.translated_text: NOTE: This section is quoted from <s>Bhagavat-sandarbha</s> 118.

body.text: (end page 13)
body.translated_text: (End of page 13)

body.text:
devatve deva-dehā sā mānuṣatve ca mānuṣī |
harer dehānurūpāṃ vai karoty eṣātmanas tanum ||53|| iti ca |
body.translated_text: In the divine form she has a divine body; in the human form she is human. She fashions her own body to correspond to the body of <s>Hari</s>. (Verse 53)

body.text: brahma-saṃhitāyāṃ (5.8) niyatiḥ sā ramā devi tat-priyā tad-vaśaṃ tadā iti | niyamyate svayaṃ bhagavaty eva niyatābhavatīti svarūpa-bhūtā śaktiḥ | devī dyotamānā prakāśa-rūpety arthaḥ | cid-rūpam iti skānde -
body.translated_text: In the <s>Brahma-saṃhitā</s> (5.8): '<s>Niyati</s> (the ordaining principle) — she is <s>Ramā Devī</s>, His beloved, under His control at that time.' She is called <s>niyati</s> because she is regulated by and devoted solely to the Lord — [thus she is] the potency inherent in His essential nature. '<s>Devī</s>' means 'the resplendent one,' i.e., she is of the nature of luminous manifestation. That she is of the nature of consciousness (<s>cit</s>) is [stated] in the <s>Skānda</s> —

children.text: aparaṃ tv akṣaraṃ yā sā prakṛtir jaḍa-rūpikā |
children.translated_text: The other, the imperishable, is that <s>Prakṛti</s> which is of inert nature;

children.text: śrīḥ parā prakṛtiḥ proktā cetanā viṣṇu-saṃśrayā ||54||
children.translated_text: <s>Śrī</s> is declared to be the transcendent <s>Prakṛti</s>, conscious, and sheltered in <s>Viṣṇu</s>. (Verse 54)

body.text: tataś ca bhagavān kṛṣṇa-saṃjña eva iti nirdhārite na viṣṇunā | vinā devītyādi devatve deva-dehā sā ity ādi tadīya-svarūpa-bhūtā īśa-vāmāṃśa-vartinī lakṣmī kim ākhyā | iti nirdhāryā | tatra dvayor api pūryoḥ śrī-mahiṣyākhyā jñeyā | tadīya-svarūpa-śaktitvaṃ skānda-parbhāsa-khaṇḍe śiva-gaurī-saṃvāde gopyādity-māhātmye dṛṣṭaṃ yathā --
body.translated_text: Therefore, it being established that the Lord is named <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> Himself — 'Without <s>Viṣṇu</s> there is no <s>Devī</s>' and 'In divine form she has a divine body' — what is the name of that <s>Lakṣmī</s> who is inherent in His essential nature and exists in the left side of the Lord? This is to be determined. For both of the two [principal forms], the designation '<s>Śrī</s>-consort' should be understood. That she is His <s>svarūpa-śakti</s> (essential potency) is seen in the <s>Skānda Purāṇa</s>, <s>Prabhāsa-khaṇḍa</s>, in the dialogue of <s>Śiva</s> and <s>Gaurī</s>, in the Glorification of the <s>Gopīs</s>, as follows —

children.text: purā kṛṣṇo mahā-tejā yadā prabhāsam āgataḥ |
children.translated_text: In ancient times, when <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> of great splendor came to <s>Prabhāsa</s>,
Accompanied by all the <s>Yādavas</s>, fifty-six <s>koṭis</s> (tens of millions) [in number],

body.text:
ṣoḍaśaiva sahasrāṇi gopyas tatra samāgatāḥ |
lakṣam ekaṃ ṣaṣṭhir ete kṛṣṇa-sutāḥ priye || ity upakramya | (end page 14)
body.translated_text: Sixteen thousand <s>gopīs</s> assembled there; one <s>lakṣa</s> (hundred thousand) and sixty — these are the sons of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, O beloved. — Thus beginning,

children.text: tato gopyo mahā devi vidyā yāḥ ṣoḍaśa smṛtāḥ |
children.translated_text: Then, O great <s>Devī</s>, those <s>gopīs</s> who are known as the sixteen <s>vidyās</s> (knowledges) —

children.text: tāsāṃ nāmāni te vakṣye tāni hy eka-manāḥ śṛṇu ||
children.translated_text: I shall tell you their names; listen with one-pointed mind.

children.text: lambinī candrikā kāntā krūrā śāntā mahodayā |
children.translated_text: <s>Lambinī</s>, <s>Candrikā</s>, <s>Kāntā</s>, <s>Krūrā</s>, <s>Śāntā</s>, <s>Mahodayā</s>,

children.text: bhīṣaṇī nandinī śokā supūrvā vimalā kṣayā ||
children.translated_text: <s>Bhīṣaṇī</s>, <s>Nandinī</s>, <s>Śokā</s>, <s>Supūrvā</s>, <s>Vimalā</s>, <s>Kṣayā</s>,

children.text: subhadrā śobhanā puṇyā haṃśītā kalāḥ kramāt |
children.translated_text: <s>Subhadrā</s>, <s>Śobhanā</s>, <s>Puṇyā</s>, and <s>Haṃsītā</s> — [these are] the <s>kalās</s> (phases) in order.

children.text: haṃsa eva yataḥ kṛṣṇaḥ paramātmā janārdanaḥ |
children.translated_text: Because <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> is the <s>Haṃsa</s> (Supreme Swan), the <s>Paramātmā</s> (Supreme Self), <s>Janārdana</s> —
These are His potencies, O <s>Devī</s>, proclaimed as exactly sixteen.

children.text: candrarūpī mataḥ kṛṣṇa kalā-rūpāstu tāḥ smṛtāḥ |
children.translated_text: <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> is regarded as moon-formed, and they are known as the <s>kalā</s>-forms (phase-forms).
The full circle of those [phases], <s>Mālinī</s>, is the sixteenth <s>kalā</s>.
Beginning from the <s>pratipat</s> (first) <s>tithi</s> (lunar day), the moon traverses through these;

children.text: ṣoḍaśaiva kalā yās tu gopī-rūpā varānane ||
children.translated_text: Those sixteen <s>kalās</s> who are in the form of <s>gopīs</s>, O beautiful-faced one —

children.text: ekaikaśas tāḥ sambhinnāḥ sahasreṇa pṛthak pṛthak |
children.translated_text: Each one of them is divided into a thousand, separately.

children.text: evaṃ te kathitaṃ devi rahasyaṃ jñāna-sambhavam |
children.translated_text: Thus has been told to you, O <s>Devī</s>, this secret born of knowledge.

children.text: ya etaṃ veda puruṣaḥ jñeyo vaiṣṇavo budhaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: The person who knows this is to be recognized by the wise as a <s>Vaiṣṇava</s>.

body.text: tatra gopyo rājñya ity arthaḥ | gopo bhūpe 'pīty amaraḥ | lambinī avatāra-śaktiḥ | haṃsaśītety atra prāptasya haṃsasya vācyam āha haṃsa eveti | sa ca candra-rūpī candra dṛṣṭāntenanoddeśya ity arthaḥ | kalā-rūpā iti tāś ca śaktayaḥ candrasyāmṛtety ādi kalā dṛṣṭāntenoddeśyā ity arthaḥ |
body.translated_text: Here '<s>gopīs</s>' means 'queens' — that is the meaning. '<s>Gopa</s>' [means] also 'king,' according to <s>Amara[kośa]</s>. '<s>Lambinī</s>' is the <s>avatāra-śakti</s> (potency of incarnation). In '<s>haṃsaśītā</s>' — the meaning of the word '<s>haṃsa</s>' obtained [through etymology] is stated as '<s>haṃsa</s> alone' [i.e., <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> Himself]. And He is 'moon-formed' — meaning He is to be illustrated through the analogy of the moon. '<s>Kalā</s>-formed' — and those potencies are to be illustrated through the analogy of the phases (<s>kalā</s>) of the moon such as '<s>amṛtā</s>' etc. — this is the meaning.

body.text:
anuktām antimāṃ mahāśaktim āha sampūrṇeti | seyaṃ tu kalā samaṣṭhirūpā jñeyā | dṛṣṭāntopādānāc candrasya tādṛśatvam āha pratipad iti | āsu etat-tulātve vivakṣitam āha ṣoḍaśaiveti | ṣoḍaśānām (end page 15) eva vidyārūpatvāt | etad-upadeśasya jñāna-sambhava-rahasyatvāt taj-jñānasya vaiṣṇavatvānumāxakaliṅgatvāc ca | krūrām īṣaṇāśokānām api bhagavat-svarūpa-bhūtānām eva satīnāṃ mallānām aśanir ity ādivat śrī-kṛṣṇasya kaṭhinatvaa-pratyāyakatvāt | mṛtur bhojapater itivat durjana-vicitrāsakatvāt | asatāṃ śāstetivat tadīya-śoka-hetutvād evaṃ ca tat-tan-niruktir upapadyate | yathā prakāśaika-rūpāyā eva sūrya-kāntor ulūkeṣu tāmisrādi-vyañjakatā | tataś candra-rūpī mata kṛṣṇaḥ kalā-rūpas tu tāḥ smṛtā iti sphuṭam eva svarūpa-bhūtatvaṃ
darśitam | tad evaṃ tāsāṃ svarūpa-śaktitve lakṣmītvaṃ tāsāṃ siddhaty eva | tad evam abhipretya tāsāṃ lakṣmītvam āha śrī-śukaḥ --
body.translated_text: He describes the final great power (<s>mahāśakti</s>) not [previously] mentioned, with the word 'complete' (<s>sampūrṇa</s>). This <s>kalā</s> (digit) should be understood as the aggregate form. That the moon is of such a nature is stated through the uptake of the illustration, with [the word] 'first day.' The intention that these are equal to that is expressed with 'sixteen only' (<s>ṣoḍaśaiva</s>). Because only the sixteen have the nature of <s>vidyā</s> (knowledge). Because the teaching of this has the nature of a secret that gives rise to knowledge, and because the knowledge thereof is an inferential mark of being a <s>Vaiṣṇava</s>. Even [the qualities] cruel (<s>krūrā</s>), jealous (<s>īṣaṇā</s>), and grief-causing (<s>aśoka</s>) — though they are indeed constitutive of the Lord's essential nature — convey <s>Śrī Kṛṣṇa</s>'s severity, as in 'a thunderbolt to the wrestlers' (<s>mallānām aśaniḥ</s>). And they convey his terrifying nature to the wicked, as in '<s>Mṛtyu</s> (Death) to <s>Bhojapati</s>.' And they are the cause of grief to such ones, as in 'the chastiser of the evil.' Thus the etymology of each is justified. Just as the <s>sūryakānta</s> (sun-stone), though of the sole nature of light, produces an appearance of darkness for owls. Therefore, '<s>Kṛṣṇa</s> is considered of the form of the moon; they [the <s>gopīs</s>] are remembered as being of the form of his digits (<s>kalā</s>)' — their being constitutive of his essential nature is clearly shown. Thus, their being <s>Lakṣmī</s> (divine fortune) is established when they are [recognized as] his <s>svarūpa-śakti</s> (essential power). Having intended this, <s>Śrī Śuka</s> declares their <s>Lakṣmī</s>-nature:

body.text:
gṛheṣu tāsām anapayyātarkya-kṛn
nirasta-sāmyātiśayeṣv avasthitaḥ |
reme ramābhir nija-kāma-sampluto
yathetaro gārhaka-medhikāṃś caran ||63|| (BhP 10.59.43)
body.translated_text: Dwelling in those homes [of his queens], where equality and superiority were completely negated, the performer of inconceivable deeds, immersed in his own desire, sported with the <s>Ramās</s> (Lakṣmīs), as though an ordinary man pursuing household life. // (<s>Bhāgavatapurāṇa</s> 10.59.43) //

body.text:
ṭīkā ca - ramābhir lakṣmyā aṃśa-bhūtābhir ity eṣā | svarūpa-śaktitvād eva reme ity uktam | ato nijaḥ striyaḥ paramānanda-śakti-viśeṣodaya-rūpa-prema-viśeṣa-svarūpo yaḥ kāmas tena sampluto vyāpta iti | tatra śrīmaty ābhāsāyāṃ bhū-śakti-rūpatvaṃ pādmottara-khaṇḍādau | yamunāyāḥ kṛpā-śakti-rūpatvaṃ skānda-yamunā-māhātmyādāv ity anveṣaṇīyam | kintu satyabhāmāyā harivaṃśādau saubhāgyāti-
(end page 16) śayasya vivakṣitatvāt prema-śakti-pracura-bhū-śaktitvaṃ jñeyam | svayaṃ lakṣmīs tu rukmiṇī |
body.translated_text: And the commentary [says]: 'with the <s>Ramās</s>' means 'with those who are partial manifestations of <s>Lakṣmī</s>.' Because they are his <s>svarūpa-śakti</s> (essential power), the word 'sported' (<s>reme</s>) is used. Therefore, 'his own' (<s>nija</s>) means: the <s>kāma</s> (desire) which is the essential nature of a special form of <s>prema</s> (divine love), characterized by the arising of a particular manifestation of supreme bliss-power — by that [desire] he was 'immersed' (<s>sampluta</s>), meaning pervaded. Regarding the blessed <s>Satyabhāmā</s> being of the nature of the <s>bhū-śakti</s> (earth-power) in the semblance [form] — this should be investigated in the <s>Padmottara-khaṇḍa</s> and elsewhere. <s>Yamunā</s>'s being of the nature of <s>kṛpā-śakti</s> (compassion-power) — [this should be investigated] in the <s>Skānda Yamunā-māhātmya</s> and elsewhere. However, since <s>Satyabhāmā</s>'s exceptional beauty is intended in the <s>Harivaṃśa</s> and elsewhere, she should be understood as the <s>bhū-śakti</s> abounding in <s>prema-śakti</s> (love-power). But <s>Rukmiṇī</s> is <s>Lakṣmī</s> herself.

children.translated_text: In <s>Dvārakā</s>, O king, there was great rejoicing among the citizens,

children.text: rukmiṇyā ramayopetaṃ dṛṣṭvā kṛṣṇaṃ śriyaḥ patim || (BhP 10.54.60)
children.translated_text: Having seen <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, the Lord of <s>Śrī</s> (Fortune), together with <s>Rukmiṇī</s>, who is <s>Ramā</s> (<s>Lakṣmī</s>). // (<s>Bhāgavatapurāṇa</s> 10.54.60) //

body.text: ity ādiṣu tasyām eva bhūriśaḥ prasiddheḥ | ataḥ svayaṃ lakṣmītvenaiva paraspara-yogyatām āha śrī-śukaḥ --
body.translated_text: In these and other [passages], her [identity as <s>Lakṣmī</s>] is abundantly well-known. Therefore <s>Śrī Śuka</s> declares their mutual suitability through her being <s>Lakṣmī</s> herself:

body.text:
asyaiva bhāryā bhavituṃ rukmiṇy arhati nāparā |
asāv apy anavadyātmā bhaiṣmyāḥ samucitaḥ patiḥ ||64|| (BhP 10.53.37)
body.translated_text: Only <s>Rukmiṇī</s> is worthy to be his wife, and no other; and he, of blameless nature, is the fitting husband for the daughter of <s>Bhīṣmaka</s>. // (<s>Bhāgavatapurāṇa</s> 10.53.37) //

body.text: *NOTE: From here to darśitavān, KṛṣṇaS 185-186, page 110. See also Gopāla-campū 15.75.
body.translated_text: NOTE: From here to 'has shown' (<s>darśitavān</s>), <s>Kṛṣṇa-sandarbha</s> 185-186, page 110. See also <s>Gopāla-campū</s> 15.75.

body.text: ataḥ svayaṃ bhagavato 'nurūpatvena svayaṃ lakṣmītvaṃ prasiddham eva | atha śrī-vṛndāvane tadīya-svarūpa-śakti-prādurbhāvāḥ śrī-vraja-devyaḥ | yathā brahma-saṃhitāyāṃ (5.37) --
body.translated_text: Therefore, her being <s>Lakṣmī</s> herself is well-established through being of a form corresponding to the Lord himself. Now, in <s>Śrī Vṛndāvana</s>, the <s>Śrī Vraja-devīs</s> (divine ladies of <s>Vraja</s>) are manifestations of his <s>svarūpa-śakti</s> (essential power). As stated in the <s>Brahma-saṃhitā</s> (5.37):

body.text:
ānanda-cinmaya-rasa-pratibhāvitābhis
tābhir ya eva nija-rūpatayā kalābhiḥ |
goloka eva nivasaty akhilātma-bhūto
govindam ādi-puruṣaṃ tam ahaṃ bhajāmi ||65|| iti |
body.translated_text: I worship that primeval Lord <s>Govinda</s>, who resides in <s>Goloka</s> alone, the Self of all beings, with those who are his own forms as <s>kalās</s> (digits), imbued with the essence of bliss and consciousness (<s>ānanda-cinmaya-rasa</s>). // (<s>Brahma-saṃhitā</s> 5.37) //

body.text: tatra tābhiḥ śrī-gopībhir mantre (5.24) tac-chabda-prayogāt | ānanda-cin-maya-rasena prema-rasa-viśeṣeṇa praitbhāvitābhis tat-pradhānābhir ity arthaḥ | hlādinī-sāra-vṛtti-viśeṣa-rūpatvāt | kalātvenaiva nija-rūpatve siddhe punar nija-rūpatayoktiḥ prakaṭa-līlāyāṃ (end page 17) parakīyābhāsatvasya vyavacchedārtham | yata uktaṃ tatraiva śriyaḥ kāntāḥ kāntaḥ parama-puruṣaḥ (5.56) iti | śrī-parama-puruṣayor aupapatyaṃ nāstīti yuktaṃ ca darśitavān | etad abhiprāyeṇaiva svāyambhuvāgame 'pi śrī-bhū-līlā-śabdaiḥ tat-preyasī-viśeṣatvam upadiṣṭam |
body.translated_text: There, 'with those' (<s>tābhiḥ</s>) refers to the <s>Śrī Gopīs</s>, because of the use of the word 'tat' (that) in the <s>mantra</s> (5.24). 'Imbued with the essence of bliss and consciousness' means: those who are predominated by a particular kind of <s>prema-rasa</s> (love-essence) — this is the meaning. Because they are of the nature of a particular manifestation of the essential function of <s>hlādinī</s> (bliss-power). Since being his own form (<s>nija-rūpatā</s>) is already established by [their nature as] <s>kalās</s> (digits), the additional statement 'as his own forms' is for the purpose of excluding the appearance of being <s>parakīya</s> (another's wife) in the manifest <s>līlā</s> (divine play). For it is stated there [in the <s>Brahma-saṃhitā</s>]: '<s>Śrīs</s> (Lakṣmīs) are his beloveds; the beloved is the Supreme Person (<s>Parama-puruṣa</s>)' (5.56). And it has been shown that illicit relationship between <s>Śrī</s> and the <s>Parama-puruṣa</s> is impossible. With this very intention, in the <s>Svāyambhuvāgama</s> also, the terms <s>Śrī</s>, <s>Bhū</s>, and <s>Līlā</s> indicate [the <s>gopīs</s>'] being particular beloveds of the Lord.

body.text:
ataiva gopījanā vidyā-kalā-preraka ity atra tāpanī-vākye śrīmad-daśākṣarastha-nāma-niruktau ye gopījanās te ā samyag yā vidyā parama-prema-rūpā tasyāḥ kalā-vṛtti-rūpā iti vyākhyeyam | rāja-vidyā rāja-guhyam ity ādi gītā-prakaraṇāt bhagavaty avidyā-saṃśleṣābhāvāt | tad uktaṃ hlādinīty ādi | tatas tāsāṃ prerakas tat krīḍāyāṃ pravartakaḥ | sa ca patitva eva viśrāntaḥ | iti vallabha-śabdenaikārthyam eva | janma-jarābhyāṃ bhinna ity ādau sa vo hi svāmī bhavati iti tasyām eva śrutau, tāḥ prati durvāsā-vākyāt | strī-sambandhe svāmī-śabdaḥ paatyāv eva rūḍhaḥ | svāmino devṛ-devarāv ity amara-koṣāt | pāda-nyāsair ity ādau [BhP 10.33.7] kṛṣṇa-vadhva iti śrī-śuka-vacanam | ṛṣabhasya jaguḥ kṛtyāni [BhP 10.33.21] ity atra ṭīkā ca ṛṣabhasya patyuḥ iti | saṅgītaśāstre
ca, gopīpatir ananto 'pi vaṃśadhvanivaśaṃ gataḥ iti. śrīmac-chaṅkarācārya-kṛte yamunāstotre ca, vidhehi tasya rādhikādhavāṅghripaṅkaje ratim iti | uddhavaṃ prati śrī-bhagavatā ca -- ballavyo me madātmikāḥ [BhP 10.46.6] iti | tad idaṃ gacchoddhava vrajaṃ saumya pitror naḥ prītim āvaha iti [BhP 10.46.3] (end page 18) vallabhābhimānitām ātmani vyajya śrīkṛṣṇasya vacanaṃ brāhmaṇasya mama brāhmaṇīty ādivat gopa-rūpasya mama gopī-rūpā ity arthaḥ | atas tāsām api tathaivābhimānaṃ tatraivoktam -- api bata madhupuryāṃ āryaputro 'dhunāste iti (10.47.11) | tathaiva ca kumārīṇāṃ saṅkalpa-vacanam - nanda-gopa-sutaṃ devi patiṃ me kurute namaḥ iti (10.22.4) |
body.translated_text: For this very reason, in the <s>Tāpanī</s> statement '<s>gopījanā vidyā-kalā-prerakaḥ</s>' — in the etymological analysis of the name within the sacred ten-syllable [<s>mantra</s>] — the <s>gopī-janas</s> (gopī-folk) should be explained as: those who are the <s>kalā</s>-form, i.e. the functional manifestation, of <s>vidyā</s>, which is the form of supreme <s>prema</s> (divine love). Because of the <s>Gītā</s> passage 'the royal knowledge, the royal secret' and similar [statements], since there is no connection with <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance) in the Lord. Thus it is said '<s>hlādinī</s>' (bliss-power) and so on. Therefore, their 'inspirer' (<s>preraka</s>) means the one who sets them in motion in their divine play (<s>krīḍā</s>). And he rests in the status of husband (<s>patitva</s>) alone. Thus there is identity of meaning with the word '<s>vallabha</s>' (beloved). In the very same <s>Śruti</s> [which says] 'He who is distinct from birth and old age,' [it is stated] 'He indeed becomes your lord (<s>svāmī</s>)' — toward them, from the words of <s>Durvāsas</s>. In the context of a woman's relationship, the word '<s>svāmī</s>' (lord) is conventionally used only for 'husband' (<s>pati</s>). [As stated] in the <s>Amarakośa</s>: '<s>Svāmin</s> [means] husband's brother and husband.' In [the passage] 'by the placement of feet' (<s>Bhāgavatapurāṇa</s> 10.33.7), there is <s>Śrī Śuka</s>'s statement '<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>'s wife.' In [the passage] 'they sang the deeds of the bull [among men]' (<s>Bhāgavatapurāṇa</s> 10.33.21), the commentary says '<s>ṛṣabhasya</s>' means 'of the husband.' And in the <s>Saṅgītaśāstra</s>: 'The husband of the <s>gopīs</s>, though infinite, came under the power of the flute's sound.' And in the <s>Yamunāstotra</s> composed by <s>Śrīmad Śaṅkarācārya</s>: 'Bestow upon me devotion to the lotus-feet of <s>Rādhikā</s>'s beloved (<s>dhava</s>).' And by the Lord himself to <s>Uddhava</s>: 'The <s>Ballavīs</s> (cowherd women) are devoted to me as their very self' (<s>Bhāgavatapurāṇa</s> 10.46.6). This statement of <s>Śrī Kṛṣṇa</s> — 'Go, <s>Uddhava</s>, to <s>Vraja</s>, O gentle one, bring joy to our parents' (<s>Bhāgavatapurāṇa</s> 10.46.3) — expressing the self-identification as beloved (<s>vallabha</s>), means: 'the <s>gopī</s>-formed ones are mine, who am of <s>gopa</s>-form' — just as a <s>brāhmaṇa</s> [says] 'my <s>brāhmaṇī</s>.' Therefore, their reciprocal self-identification is also stated there: 'Does the noble son now dwell in <s>Mathurā</s>?' [using] '<s>āryaputra</s>' (noble husband) (<s>Bhāgavatapurāṇa</s> 10.47.11). And likewise the vow-statement of the maidens (<s>kumārīs</s>): 'O <s>Devī</s>, make the son of <s>Nanda Gopa</s> my husband, I bow.' (<s>Bhāgavatapurāṇa</s> 10.22.4).

body.text: na kevalaṃ sādhāraṇa-rītyā dāmpatya-vyavahāras tābhir mama kintu mad-ātmikā mat-svarūpa-śaktaya ity arthaḥ | ātma-śabdasya manīvācakatvena tā man-manaskā (10.46.4) ity ādy uktaṃ punar uktaṃ syāt | uktaṃ ca tāsāṃ svarūpa-śaktitvaṃ śrī-śukadevena -
body.translated_text: Not merely in the ordinary sense is there conjugal relationship with them, but [the meaning is:] they are '<s>mad-ātmikāḥ</s>' — 'of my essential nature,' meaning 'my <s>svarūpa-śaktis</s>' (essential powers). Since the word '<s>ātma</s>' can denote the mind, [the statement] 'they whose minds are fixed on me' (<s>Bhāgavatapurāṇa</s> 10.46.4) and similar would become redundant. And <s>Śrī Śukadev</s> has declared their being <s>svarūpa-śakti</s>:

body.text:
tābhir vidhuta-śokābhir bhagavān acyuto vṛtaḥ |
vyarocatādhikaṃ tāta puruṣaḥ śaktibhir yathā || iti | (10.32.10)
body.translated_text: The Lord <s>Acyuta</s>, surrounded by those [<s>gopīs</s>] whose grief was dispelled, shone forth all the more — O dear one, just as <s>Puruṣa</s> (the Supreme Person) [shines] with his <s>Śaktis</s> (powers). // (<s>Bhāgavatapurāṇa</s> 10.32.10) //

body.text: tābhiḥ śaktibhir yathā yāvat tathā tatrātiśuśubhe tābhir bhagavān devakī-sutaḥ ity ādi | cakāśa gopī-pariṣad-gato 'rcita ity ādi | vyarocataiṇāṅka ivoḍubhir vṛta ity ādi | svarūpa-śaktitvād evādhikaṃ vyarocata ity ādy-uktam upapadyate | sva-śaktyeka-prakāśat śrī-bhagavataḥ | atas tāsāṃ lakṣmī-saṃjñatvam apy uktaṃ brahma-saṃhitāyāṃ lakṣmī-sahasra-śata-sambhrama-sevyamānam iti | śriyaḥ kāntāḥ kāntaḥ parama-puruṣa iti | śrī-daśame ca --
body.translated_text: 'With those <s>śaktis</s>' — to the extent that, thus in that [passage] he was supremely resplendent — 'the Lord, son of <s>Devakī</s>, [shone] with them' and so on; 'he shone in the assembly of the <s>gopīs</s>, worshiped' and so on; 'he shone like the moon surrounded by stars' and so on. Because they are his <s>svarūpa-śakti</s>, the statement 'he shone forth all the more' and similar are justified. Because the Lord manifests only through his own power. Therefore, their designation as <s>Lakṣmī</s> is also stated in the <s>Brahma-saṃhitā</s>: 'served with eagerness by hundreds of thousands of <s>Lakṣmīs</s>.' And: '<s>Śrīs</s> (Lakṣmīs) are the beloveds; the beloved is the Supreme Person.' And in the tenth [canto of the <s>Bhāgavata</s>]:

body.text: (end page 19) gopyo labdhvācyutaṃ kāntaṃ śriya ekānta-vallabham iti (10.33.14) gopya eva śriya kāntaṃ manoharaṃ ekānta-vallabhaṃ raho-ramaṇam | tasmāt nāyaṃ śriyo 'ṅga iti śukānuvādaḥ sāmānye lakṣmī-vijayaṃ vyanakti | lakṣmī-sahasreti viriñca-vāṇī lakṣmī-viśeṣatvam urīkaroti | kurutve 'pi śrī-yudhiṣṭhirādīnāṃ pāṇḍava-saṃjñatvam | lakṣmītve 'pi vraja-devīnāṃ gopī-saṃjñatvam iti | tasmāt tāsāṃ parama-lakṣmī-rūpatvena tan-nitya-preyasītvaṃ siddham |
body.translated_text: 'The <s>gopīs</s>, having obtained <s>Acyuta</s> as their beloved — the exclusive darling of <s>Śrī</s> (Fortune)' (<s>Bhāgavatapurāṇa</s> 10.33.14). 'The <s>gopīs</s> indeed — [obtained] the charming one, the exclusive darling of <s>Śrī</s> (Fortune), as their secret paramour.' Therefore, <s>Śuka</s>'s subsequent statement 'He is not [the property] of <s>Śrī</s>, O friend' indicates [his] superiority over <s>Lakṣmī</s> in the general [sense]. <s>Brahmā</s>'s declaration 'hundreds of thousands of <s>Lakṣmīs</s>' confirms [their] being particular [forms of] <s>Lakṣmī</s>. Just as the sons of <s>Pāṇḍu</s>, including <s>Śrī Yudhiṣṭhira</s>, have the designation '<s>Pāṇḍava</s>' [as a group name], so too the ladies of <s>Vraja</s>, though being <s>Lakṣmīs</s>, have the designation '<s>gopī</s>.' Therefore, their being the supreme <s>Lakṣmī</s>-forms establishes their being the Lord's eternal beloveds.

body.text: tathā ca gautamīya-tantre daśārṇa-vyākhyāyām (20-21) --
body.translated_text: And accordingly, in the <s>Gautamīya-tantra</s>, in the explanation of the ten-syllable [<s>mantra</s>] (20-21):

children.translated_text: One should know '<s>gopī</s>' as <s>Prakṛti</s> (primordial nature); '<s>jana</s>' [denotes] the totality of <s>tattvas</s> (principles);
The Lord is the support of both through pervading and through being their cause. // 67 //
The concentrated bliss, the supreme light, is spoken of as the 'beloved' (<s>vallabha</s>);
Or alternatively, '<s>gopī</s>' is <s>Prakṛti</s>; '<s>jana</s>' is the circle of her portions (<s>aṃśa</s>). // 68 //

body.text:
anayor vallabhaḥ proktaḥ svāmī kṛṣṇākhya īśvaraḥ|
kāryakāraṇayor īśaḥ śrutibhis tena gīyate||69||
body.translated_text: Their beloved is declared to be the Lord, the master called <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>; the Lord of cause and effect is thus sung by the <s>Śrutis</s> (scriptures). // 69 //

body.text:
anekajanmasiddhānāṃ gopīnāṃ patir eva vā|
nandanandana ity uktas trailokyānandavardhanaḥ||70|| iti.
body.translated_text: Or, <s>Nandanandana</s> (the son of <s>Nanda</s>), the increaser of the bliss of the three worlds, is declared to be the husband of the <s>gopīs</s> whose [realization was] perfected through many births. // 70 // Thus.

body.text: ataiva prathamā prakṛtiḥ pradhānaṃ | dvitīyā svarūpa-śaktiḥ | tattvāni mahad-ādīni aṃśāḥ |
body.translated_text: Thus, the first <s>prakṛti</s> (nature) is <s>pradhāna</s> (primordial matter). The second is <s>svarūpa-śakti</s> (the intrinsic potency). The <s>tattvas</s> (principles) such as <s>mahat</s> (the great principle) and so forth are its parts.

children.translated_text: <s>Jñāna</s> (knowledge), <s>śakti</s> (potency), <s>bala</s> (strength), <s>aiśvarya</s> (sovereignty), <s>vīrya</s> (heroism), and <s>tejas</s> (splendor) — in their entirety,
are denoted by the word <s>Bhagavat</s> (the Lord), without the objectionable qualities such as the <s>guṇas</s> (material qualities) and so forth. (71)

body.text: iti viṣṇu-purāṇoktāḥ (ViP 6.5.79) |
body.translated_text: Thus it is stated in the <s>Viṣṇu Purāṇa</s> (ViP 6.5.79).

body.text:
atra anekajanmasiddhānāṃ iti, bahūni me vyatītāni (end page 20) janmāni tava cārjuna [bg 4.5] itivat anādi-siddhatvam eva bodhayati | patir eva ity eva-kāreṇa prakaṭa-līlāyām upapatitva-vyavahāras tu māyika evety arthaḥ | sa cāgre darśayiṣyate | vā-śabdasyaivottara-pakṣatā-bodhanāya |
[*NOTE: GCP 15.73-75]
body.translated_text: Here, the phrase "of those perfected over many births" indicates eternal perfection, just as "Many births of Mine have passed, and of yours too, O <s>Arjuna</s>" (BG 4.5) indicates beginningless perfection. By the emphatic particle "eva" in "the husband alone," it is meant that the designation of paramour-hood in the manifest <s>līlā</s> (divine play) is merely illusory — that is the meaning. This will be demonstrated further on. The particle "vā" is used to indicate the subsequent alternative position.

body.text: tad evam ādibhir viśiṣṭatvenaiva tad-ārādhanād āsāṃ nitya-preyasītvaṃ siddham | tac-chṛtīnāṃ tad-ārādhānāṃ cānāghananatabhāvitvāt | sa hi mantre caturdhā pratīyate | mantrasya kāraṇa-rūpatvena varṇa-samudāya-rūpatvena, adhiṣṭhātṛ-devatā-rūpatvena ārādhya-rūpatvena ca | atra kāraṇa-rūpatvaṃ tad-adhiṣṭhātṛ-devatā-rūpatvaṃ coktaṃ brahma-saṃhitāyāṃ prakṛtyā puruṣeṇa ca iti (5.3) | prakṛtir mantrasya svarūpas trayam eva śrī-kṛṣṇaḥ kāraṇa-rūpatvāt | tad evoktam ṛṣy-ādi-smaraṇe kṛṣṇaḥ prakṛtir iti | sa eva adhiṣṭhātṛ-devatā-rūpaḥ | varṇa-samudāya-rūpaṃ coktaṃ tatraiva - kāmaḥ kṛṣṇāyety (BrahmaS 5.24) ādinā | uktaṃ ca hayaśīrṣa-pañcarātre
body.translated_text: Thus, through worship of Him with such distinguishing qualities as described above, their status as eternal beloveds is established, since those <s>śrutis</s> (scriptures) and those acts of worship are never devoid of this character. For the <s>mantra</s> is understood in four aspects: as having the nature of cause, as being a collection of syllables, as having the nature of the presiding deity, and as having the nature of the deity to be worshipped. Here, the nature as cause and the nature as presiding deity are stated in the <s>Brahma-saṃhitā</s>: "by <s>prakṛti</s> (nature) and <s>puruṣa</s> (person)" (5.3). <s>Prakṛti</s> is the essential nature of the <s>mantra</s>; all three are none other than <s>Śrī Kṛṣṇa</s>, since He is the cause. Thus it is said: "In the recollection of the <s>ṛṣi</s> (seer) and so forth, <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> is <s>prakṛti</s>." He Himself is in the form of the presiding deity. The nature as a collection of syllables is also stated there — "<s>kāmaḥ kṛṣṇāya</s>" (<s>Brahma-saṃhitā</s> 5.24) and so forth. And it is said in the <s>Hayaśīrṣa Pañcarātra</s>:

body.text:
vācyatvaṃ vācakatvaṃ ca devatā-mantrayor hi |
abhedenocyate grahma tattvavidbhir vicārataḥ || iti |
body.translated_text: The relation of signified and signifier between the deity and the <s>mantra</s>, indeed, is declared as non-different by the knowers of truth upon deliberation.

body.text: ārādhya-rūpatvaṃ ca tatraiva brahma-saṃhitāyāṃ -- īśvaraḥ paramaḥ kṛṣṇaḥ saccidānanda-vigrahaḥ | anādir ādir ity ādinā (5.1) kvicid durgāyā adhiṣṭhātṛtvaṃ tu śakti-śaktimator abheda-vivakṣayā | ata uktaṃ gautamīya-kalpe - yaḥ kṛṣṇaḥ saiva durgā syād yā durgā kṛṣṇa eva sa iti | yataḥ śrī-kṛṣṇas tatra svarūpa-śakti-rūpeṇa durgā nāma | tasmān neyaṃ māyāṃśa-bhūtā durgā iti gamyate | niruktiś cātra duḥkhena (end page 21) gurv-ārādhanādi-prayāsena gamyate jñāyate iti | tathā ca nārada-pañcarātre śruti-vidyā-saṃvāde -
body.translated_text: The nature as the deity to be worshipped is also stated there in the <s>Brahma-saṃhitā</s> — "<s>Kṛṣṇa</s> is the supreme Lord, whose form is <s>saccidānanda</s> (existence-consciousness-bliss), without beginning, the origin of all" (5.1) and so forth. In some places, the presiding status of <s>Durgā</s> is stated with the intention of expressing the non-difference of <s>śakti</s> (potency) and <s>śaktimān</s> (the possessor of potency). Therefore it is said in the <s>Gautamīya Kalpa</s>: "He who is <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> is indeed <s>Durgā</s>; she who is <s>Durgā</s> is <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> Himself." Because <s>Śrī Kṛṣṇa</s> is there in the form of <s>svarūpa-śakti</s> (intrinsic potency) named <s>Durgā</s>. Therefore, she is not to be understood as the <s>Durgā</s> who is a portion of <s>māyā</s> (illusion). And the etymology here is: she who is known (<s>gamyate</s>) through difficulty (<s>duḥkhena</s>), that is, through the arduous effort of worshipping the <s>guru</s> (spiritual master) and so forth. And thus in the <s>Nārada Pañcarātra</s>, in the dialogue between <s>Śruti</s> and <s>Vidyā</s>:

children.text: jānāty ekā parā kāntaṃ saiva durgā tad-ātmikā |
children.translated_text: One supreme beloved alone knows the Lord — she is <s>Durgā</s>, identical with Him.
She who is the supreme potency of the Supreme, embodying <s>Mahāviṣṇu</s> Himself,
by the mere knowledge of whom, the attainment of the Supreme Self,

children.text: muhūrtād eva devasya prāptir bhavati nānyathā ||
children.translated_text: of the Lord, occurs within a moment and not otherwise.
This one <s>Śrī Gokuleśvarī</s> (the Queen of <s>Gokula</s>) is by nature the totality of <s>prema</s> (divine love).
Through her, the primeval Lord, the master of all, is easily known.
<s>Bhakti</s> (devotion), the wealth of <s>bhajana</s> (worship) — <s>prakṛti</s> (the potency) worships her beloved.
She is known through the most extreme difficulty — this <s>prakṛti</s> of the Self,
is sung by all as <s>Durgā</s>, the beloved of undivided <s>rasa</s> (divine rapture).

body.text:
asyā āvarikā śaktir mahāmāyā 'khileśvarī |
yayā mugdhaṃ jagat sarvaṃ sarva-dehābhimāninaḥ || iti |
body.translated_text: Her covering potency is <s>Mahāmāyā</s> (the great illusion), the ruler of all, by whom the entire world is bewildered, all beings identifying with their bodies.

body.text: ataiva māyāṃ vyudasya cic-chaktyā kaivalye sthita ātmanīti prathamokteḥ | na yatra māyā kim utāpare harer iti dvitīyokteḥ māyātīta-vaikuṇṭhāvaraṇa-kathane yathoktaṃ pādmottara-khaṇḍe -
body.translated_text: For this very reason, the first statement says "having cast aside <s>māyā</s> (illusion), established in oneness through <s>cit-śakti</s> (the spiritual potency) in the Self"; and the second statement says "where there is no <s>māyā</s>, what to speak of others belonging to <s>Hari</s>." In the description of the covering of <s>Vaikuṇṭha</s>, which transcends <s>māyā</s>, it is stated in the <s>Padma Purāṇa</s>, Uttara-khaṇḍa:

children.translated_text: <s>Satya</s>, <s>Acyuta</s>, <s>Ananta</s>, <s>Durgā</s>, <s>Viṣvaksena</s>, and <s>Gajānana</s>,

children.text: śaṅkha-padma-nidhī lokāś caturthāvaraṇaṃ smṛtam || ity ady uktvā -
children.translated_text: <s>Śaṅkha</s> and <s>Padma</s> (the two treasures), and the worlds — these are known as the fourth covering. Having stated this and so forth —

children.text: nityāḥ sarve pare dhāmni ye cānye 'pi divaukasaḥ |
children.translated_text: All those who are eternal in the supreme abode, and whatever other celestial beings there are,
they in this material heaven are indeed impermanent, the lords of the three worlds.

body.text: iti teṣāṃ śrī-bhagavad-aṃśa-rūpatvam uktaṃ trailokya-sammohana-tantre --
body.translated_text: Thus their nature as forms and portions of <s>Śrī Bhagavān</s> (the Supreme Lord) is stated in the <s>Trailokya-sammohana Tantra</s>:

children.translated_text: Everywhere, the God of gods,
<s>Hari</s>, dressed in the garb of a cowherd,
merely through difference of form,
difference of name is proclaimed. (77)

body.text: ato nāma-mātra-sādhāreṇe 'nanya-bhaktair na vibhetavyaṃ kintu bhāgavatair nitya-vaikuṇṭha-sevakatvāt viṣvaksenādivat sat-kāryā eva te | arcayitvā tu govindaṃ tadīyān nārcayet tu yaḥ ity ādi-vacanena tad-asatkāre doṣa-śravaṇāt | ataiva tān evoddiśya uktam ekādaśe -
body.translated_text: Therefore, those who have exclusive devotion should not be apprehensive about the mere commonality of names. Rather, since they are eternal servants of <s>Vaikuṇṭha</s>, they should be honored like <s>Viṣvaksena</s> and others, by the devotees of <s>Bhagavān</s>. Because there is the scriptural statement of fault in disrespecting them, as in: "One who, having worshipped <s>Govinda</s>, does not worship those who belong to Him..." and so forth. For this very reason, it is stated in the Eleventh Canto with reference to them:

body.text:
durgāṃ vināyakaṃ vyāsaṃ
viṣvaksenaṃ gurūn surān |
sve sve sthāne tv abhimukhān
pūjayet prokṣaṇādibhiḥ ||78|| (BhP 11.27.29)
body.translated_text: One should worship <s>Durgā</s>, <s>Vināyaka</s>, <s>Vyāsa</s>, <s>Viṣvaksena</s>, the <s>gurus</s> (spiritual masters), and the <s>devas</s> (gods), each in their respective places, facing them, with sprinkling of water and other rites. (78) (<s>Bhāgavata Purāṇa</s> 11.27.29)

body.text: atha prakṛtam anusarāmaḥ | sad eva śrī-gopīnāṃ svarūpa-śaktitve prasiddhe śrī-kṛṣṇasya nitya-preyasī-rūpatvaṃ siddham eva | tatas tābhiḥ saha tasya pūjana āvaśyakatā svataḥ siddhā | atra punaḥ prativādī prāha, yadi tāḥ kṛṣṇasya nitya-priyāḥ, tarhi kathaṃ parakīyārūpatvam | tatrāpi putrādi-saṃyoktṛtvaṃ śrūyate | satyaṃ tad-rūpatvaṃ māyikam iti vaiṣṇava-toṣaṇī-nāmnyāṃ śrī-daśama-ṭippanyāṃ kṛṣṇa-sandarbhādau ca pramitam iti vistara-bhayān nātra prapañcitam |
body.translated_text: Now let us return to the main topic. When the nature of <s>Śrī Gopīs</s> as <s>svarūpa-śakti</s> (intrinsic potency) is well-established, their status as the eternal beloveds of <s>Śrī Kṛṣṇa</s> is indeed established. From that, the necessity of worshipping Him together with them is self-evident. Here again the objector says: if they are the eternal beloveds of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, then how can they have the appearance of belonging to others (<s>parakīya</s>)? And moreover, the connection with sons and so forth is heard of regarding them. True — that form of theirs is illusory (<s>māyika</s>), as has been demonstrated in the commentary named <s>Vaiṣṇava-toṣaṇī</s> on the Tenth Canto, and in the <s>Kṛṣṇa-sandarbha</s> and elsewhere. Out of fear of excessive length, this is not elaborated here.

body.text: atha sāmānyataḥ śrī-kṛṣṇa-priyāḥ khalu dvidhā | nitya-siddhāḥ sādhana-siddhāś ca | tatra nitya-siddhāḥ pūrvoktiḥ | sādhana-siddhāś ca trividhāḥ | ṛṣijāḥ śrutayo deva-kanyāś ca | tatra ṛṣijā yathā pādmottara-khaṇḍe --
body.translated_text: Now, in general, the beloveds of <s>Śrī Kṛṣṇa</s> are indeed of two kinds: <s>nitya-siddha</s> (eternally perfected) and <s>sādhana-siddha</s> (perfected through practice). Among these, the <s>nitya-siddhas</s> have been described previously. The <s>sādhana-siddhas</s> are of three kinds: <s>ṛṣi</s>-born (born from sages), <s>śrutis</s> (personified Vedic scriptures), and daughters of the <s>devas</s> (gods). Among these, the <s>ṛṣi</s>-born are described in the <s>Padma Purāṇa</s>, Uttara-khaṇḍa:

body.text: (end 23)

children.translated_text: Formerly, all the great sages dwelling in the <s>Daṇḍakāraṇya</s> (Daṇḍaka forest),
