children.text: dṛṣṭvā rāmaṃ hariṃ tatra bhoktum aicchan suvigraham ||79||
children.translated_text: having seen <s>Rāma</s>, who is <s>Hari</s> Himself, desired to enjoy His beautiful form. (79)

children.text: te sarve strītvam āpannāḥ samudbhūtāś ca gokule |
children.translated_text: They all attained womanhood and were born in <s>Gokula</s>,

children.text: hariṃ samprāpya kāmena tato muktā bhavārṇavāt ||80||
children.translated_text: and having attained <s>Hari</s> through desire, they were then liberated from the ocean of material existence. (80)

body.text: na ca vaktavyaṃ gokula-jātānāṃ prāpañcika-dehāditvaṃ na sambhavatīti | avatāra-līlāyāḥ prāpañcika-miśratvāt | śrī-devakī devyām api ṣaḍ-garbha-saṃjñakānāṃ janma śrūyate iti |
body.translated_text: And it should not be objected that those born in <s>Gokula</s> cannot have material bodies and so forth, since the <s>līlā</s> (divine play) of the <s>avatāra</s> (incarnation) involves admixture with the material realm. Even in the divine mother <s>Śrī Devakī</s>, the birth of those known as the six embryos is heard of.

body.text: śrutayo yathā bṛhad-vāmana-purāṇādiṣu śrūyante | yata eva tathā vyākhyātaṃ striya urugendra-bhoga-bhuja-daṇḍa-viṣakta-dhiyo vayam apīti (BhP 10.87.23) | gāyatrī ca tāsu jāteti pādme sṛṣṭi-khaṇḍe yathā brahmaṇā gopa-kanyāyā gāyatryā udvāhe gopeṣu śrī-viṣṇu-vākyam -
body.translated_text: The <s>śrutis</s> (personified Vedic scriptures) are described as such in the <s>Bṛhad-vāmana Purāṇa</s> and other texts. Because of this, it has been explained thus regarding the verse "O greatest of beings, we too, whose minds are attached to the arms of your serpentine embrace" (<s>Bhāgavata Purāṇa</s> 10.87.23). And <s>Gāyatrī</s> too was born among them, as stated in the <s>Padma Purāṇa</s>, Sṛṣṭi-khaṇḍa, where <s>Śrī Viṣṇu</s> speaks at the wedding of the cowherd girl <s>Gāyatrī</s> performed by <s>Brahmā</s>:

body.text:
mayā jñātvā tataḥ kanyā dattā caiṣāviriñcaye |
yuṣmākaṃ ca kule cāhaṃ deva-kāryārtha-siddhaye |
avatāraṃ kariṣyāmi mat-kāntā tu bhaviṣyati || iti |
body.translated_text: "Having known her, I then gave this maiden to <s>Viriñcaya</s> (<s>Brahmā</s>). And in your clan, for the purpose of accomplishing the work of the gods, I shall incarnate, and she shall be My beloved."

body.text: deva-kanyāś ca yathā śrī-daśame tat-priyārthaṃ sambhavantu sura-striya iti (BhP 10.1.13) | ata sura-striyas tāsāṃ śrī-kṛṣṇa-priyāṇām upayogāyeveti gamyate | atas tat-priyārtham ity evoktaṃ, na tu tat-prīty-artham iti |
body.translated_text: The daughters of the <s>devas</s> (gods) are described in the Tenth Canto of <s>Śrī Bhāgavata</s>: "Let the wives of the gods take birth for His pleasure" (<s>Bhāgavata Purāṇa</s> 10.1.13). Therefore it is understood that the wives of the gods were for the purpose of serving as beloveds of <s>Śrī Kṛṣṇa</s>. Hence it is said "for His beloved" (<s>tat-priyārtham</s>), not "for His pleasure" (<s>tat-prīty-artham</s>).

body.text: atas tāsāṃ caturvidhatvam uktaṃ pādme -
body.translated_text: Therefore, their fourfold nature is stated in the <s>Padma Purāṇa</s>:

children.text: gopyas tu ṛṣijā gopa-kanyakāḥ śrutijāḥ parāḥ |
children.translated_text: The <s>gopīs</s> are: those born from <s>ṛṣis</s> (sages), the cowherd maidens, those born from <s>śrutis</s> (Vedic scriptures) who are supreme,

children.text: deva-kanyāś ca rājendra na mānuṣyaḥ kadācana ||
children.translated_text: and daughters of the <s>devas</s> (gods), O king of kings — never are they ordinary human women.

body.text: (end page 24)
gopa-kanyā eva nityāḥ | na mānuṣaḥ kathañcaneti praākṛta-mānuṣya-niṣedhāt | atas tāsāṃ svarūpa-śaktitvād eva śrī-bhagavatas tābhiḥ saha riraṃsā jātā | yathā śrī-śukaḥ |
body.translated_text: The cowherd maidens alone are the eternal ones. The statement "never human in any way" negates ordinary material humanity. Therefore, because they are <s>svarūpa-śakti</s> (the intrinsic potency) itself, the desire for amorous play with them arose in <s>Śrī Bhagavān</s> (the Supreme Lord). As <s>Śrī Śuka</s> says:

body.text: bhagavān api tā rātrīḥ śaradotphullamallikāḥ

children.translated_text: set His mind upon enjoying, taking recourse to <s>Yogamāyā</s> (the divine potency of illusion). (<s>Bhāgavata Purāṇa</s> 10.29.1)

body.translated_text: <s>Bhagavān</s> (the Supreme Lord) too, seeing those nights with <s>mallikā</s> (jasmine) flowers blooming in autumn,

body.text: tā rātrīr vīkṣya uddīpanatvenānubhūyeti kaumutyenālambana-rūpāṇāṃ tāsāṃ prema-mahimā darśitaḥ | ātmārāmāś ca munayaḥ ity ādau itthambhūta-guṇo harir itivat itthambhūta-guṇās tāḥ yena tādṛśy api tasya ramaṇcchā jāyate iti | ataiva vyavahārārthaṃ tasya kaiśoram api mānitaṃ jātam iti śrī-viṣṇu-purāṇe darśitam |
body.translated_text: "Seeing those nights" means experiencing them as stimulants (<s>uddīpana</s>); through the word "<s>kaumudī</s>" (moonlight), the glory of <s>prema</s> (divine love) of those <s>gopīs</s>, who are the <s>ālambana</s> (foundational cause), is shown. Just as in the verse beginning "Even the self-satisfied sages" the expression "<s>Hari</s> has such qualities" (<s>itthambhūta-guṇa</s>) is used, similarly they possess such qualities that even in one such as Him, the desire for amorous play arises. For this very reason, it is shown in the <s>Viṣṇu Purāṇa</s> that His adolescence was also honored for the sake of the <s>līlā</s> (divine play):

body.text: so 'pi kaiśoraka-vayo mānayan madhusūdanaḥ |

children.text: reme tābhir ameyātmā kṣapāsu kṣaptāhitaḥ || (ViP 5.13.60) iti |
children.translated_text: of immeasurable Self, sported with them during the nights, the destroyer of enemies. (<s>Viṣṇu Purāṇa</s> 5.13.60)

body.translated_text: He too, <s>Madhusūdana</s> (the slayer of <s>Madhu</s>), honoring adolescent age,

body.text: harivaṃśe ca-
body.translated_text: And in the <s>Harivaṃśa</s>:

body.text: yuvatīr gopa-kanyāś ca rātrau saṅkālya kālavit |

children.text: kaiśorakaṃ mānayānaḥ saha tābhir mumoda ca || (HV 63.18) iti |
children.translated_text: honoring the age of adolescence, rejoiced together with them. (<s>Harivaṃśa</s> 63.18)

body.translated_text: The knower of time, having gathered the young cowherd maidens at night,

body.text: atra kālavid ity asya vyākhyānaṃ tā rātrīr vikṣyeti | saha tābhir mumoda hetyasya sūcakaṃ rantuṃ manaś cakre iti | ity ālambana-kāla-deśānāṃ śrī-kṛṣṇāya parama-puruṣatvaṃ darśitaṃ tasmāt hlādinī-śakti-vilāsa-lakṣaṇa-tat-prema-mayy evaiṣā riraṃsā | na tu prākṛta-kāmamayīti | śrī-svāmibhir api vyaktam uktaṃ dvātriṃśe virahālāpa-viklinna-hṛdayo harir iti sva-premāmṛta-kallola-vihvalī-kṛta-cetasa iti | ataiva tac-chravaṇa-phala-dvārā tad-arcanasyāvaśyakatāṃ darśayati śrīman-munīndraḥ ||
body.translated_text: Here, the explanation of '<s>kālavid</s>' (knower of time) is 'seeing those nights.' The indication of 'he delighted together with them' is 'his mind turned to sport.' Thus, regarding the support (<s>ālambana</s>), time, and place of <s>Śrī Kṛṣṇa</s>'s...

body.text: (end page 25)
body.translated_text: (end page 25)

body.text:
vikrīḍitaṃ vraja-vadhūbhir idaṃ ca viṣṇoḥ
śraddhānvito yaḥ śṛṇuyād atha varṇayed vā
bhaktiṃ parāṃ bhagavati parilabhya kāmaṃ
hṛd-rogam āśv apahinoty acireṇa dhīraḥ || (BhP 10.33.42) iti ||84
body.translated_text:
'This sport of <s>Viṣṇu</s> with the young women of <s>Vraja</s> —
whoever hears or describes it with faith
obtains supreme devotion to the Lord;
quickly they cast off the heart's disease of lust.' (<s>Bhāgavata Purāṇa</s> 10.33.39)

body.text: atra sva-priyābhiḥ saṃvalitasya śrī-kṛṣṇasya krīḍāyāḥ śravaṇa-varṇana-mātreṇa bahu-sādhana-duḥsādhyāpi parā bhaktir udayate udaya-mātreṇa ca hṛd-rogaḥ śīghram apahriyate iti hi spaṣṭam eveti phalātiśaya-kathanena pravartanāt vidhitvam eva sidhyati | yasya parṇamayī juhur bhavati na sa pāpaṃ ślokaṃ śṛṇotītivat | na cādhikārī kaniṣṭha iti vācyaṃ dhīra ity uktatvāt |
body.translated_text: Here, merely by hearing and describing the play of <s>Śrī Kṛṣṇa</s> united with his beloveds, supreme devotion (<s>parā bhakti</s>), which is difficult to attain even through many spiritual practices, arises; and merely by its arising, the disease of the heart...

body.text: atha darśana-mantre nāmāntareṇānirdiśya śrī-vallavīnāṃ nāma viśeṣam ālambyaiva svayaṃ bhagavato nirdeśāt tāsāṃ tat-paricāyakāṅga-rūpatvam eva bodhitam | gopī-gopa-paśūnāṃ bahiḥ smared asya gīrvāṇa-ghaṭām ity ādi krama-dīpikāyāṃ (KD 3.32) gautamīya-tantre -
body.translated_text: Now, in the <s>darśana-mantra</s> (vision-<s>mantra</s>), rather than indicating [the <s>gopīs</s>] by any other name, the Blessed Lord himself designates them specifically by the name '<s>vallavī</s>' (cowherd women), thus making known that they are limbs that reveal him.

children.translated_text: Dark as a fresh rain-cloud, with eyes like blue lotuses,

children.text: vallavī-nandanaṃ vande kṛṣṇaṃ gopāla-rūpiṇam ||85 ity ādau -
children.translated_text: I salute <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, the delight of the <s>vallavīs</s>, in the form of a cowherd. (85) — thus at the beginning:
With the sweet sounds of the flute placed upon his beautiful lips,
Delighting the minds of the radiant cowherd women again and again. (86)

body.text:
vallavī-vadanāmbhoja-madhupāna-madhu-vratam |
kṣobhayantaṃ manas tāsāṃ susmerāpāṅgavīkṣaṇaiḥ ||87|| (end page 26)
yauvanodbhinna-dehābhiḥ saṃsaktābhiḥ parasparam |
vicitrāmbara-bhūṣābhir gopa-nārībhir āvṛtam ||87|| iti |
body.translated_text:
A bee [eager] for the honey-drinking from the lotus-faces of the <s>vallavīs</s>,
agitating their minds with his smiling sidelong glances. (87) (end page 26)
With women whose bodies blossomed in youth, closely embraced...

body.text: atra sā tvāṃ brahman nṛpa-vadhūḥ kāmam āśu bhajiṣyatīti [BhP 3.21.28] kardamaṃ prati śrī-śukla-vacanavac ca gopa-jātibhir nārībhir ity arthaḥ |
body.translated_text: Here, [the words] 'she, O <s>Brahman</s>, the princess, will quickly worship you with desire' (<s>Bhāgavata Purāṇa</s> 3.21.28) — just as the words of <s>Śrī Śukla</s> to <s>Kardama</s> — the meaning is: by women of the cowherd caste.

body.text: kṣobhayantaṃ mohayantaṃ muhur muhur iti vartamāna-dvaya-prayogena nityam eva tad-upāsakaiḥ paṭhyamāna-stavena gopī-kṛṣṇayoḥ nityatvam eva lakṣyate | sanat-kumāra-kalpe ca gopāṅganā parivṛtaṃ mūle kalpataroḥ sthitam ity ādi | rudra-yāmalasya śauri-tantre gopī-go-gopa-vīto ruru-nakha-vilasat-kaṇṭha-bhūṣaś ciraṃ naḥ ity ādi | mṛtyu-sañjaya-tantre -
body.translated_text: By the use of the two present participles '<s>kṣobhayantam</s>' (agitating) and '<s>mohayantam</s>' (enchanting) along with '<s>muhur muhuḥ</s>' (again and again), the eternality of the <s>gopīs</s> and <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> is indicated through the hymn constantly recited by their worshipers...

body.text:
smared vṛndāvane ramye mohayantam anāratam |
vallavī-vallabhaṃ kṛṣṇaṃ gopa-kanyā-sahasraśaḥ || ity ādi |
body.translated_text:
'One should meditate in the beautiful <s>Vṛndāvana</s> upon him who perpetually enchants,
<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, the beloved of the <s>vallavīs</s>, among thousands of cowherd girls.' — and so on.

body.text:
phullendīvara-kāntim ity ādi evaṃ svāyambhuvāgamādāv api |
[*NOTE: KK 3.82; KṛṣṇaS 106 (p49fn) attributed to Mṛtyu-sañjaya-tantra. Padyāvalī 46, attributed to Śaradākara.]
body.translated_text: 'Of the beauty of a blooming blue lotus' and so on — likewise in the <s>Svāyambhuva Āgama</s> and other [texts]. [*NOTE: <s>Kṛṣṇa-karṇāmṛta</s> 3.82; <s>Kṛṣṇa Sandarbha</s> 106 (p49fn) attributed to <s>Mṛtyu-sañjaya-tantra</s>. <s>Padyāvalī</s> 46...]

body.text: punaḥ prativādī prāha bhavatu nāma tāḥ pūjyāḥ | kintu tāsāṃ nāma kutrāpi na śrutam | tatrāpi bhaviṣyottare malla-dvādaśī-prasaṅge śrī-kṛṣṇa-yudhiṣṭhira-saṃvāde -

children.translated_text: 'O king of kings, learn from me the names of the <s>gopīs</s> in order of importance:
<s>Gopālī</s>, <s>Pālikā</s>, <s>Dhanyā</s>, <s>Viśākhā</s>, <s>Dhyānaniṣṭhikā</s>,
<s>Rādhā</s>, <s>Anurādhā</s>, <s>Somābhā</s>, <s>Tārakā</s>, and <s>Daśamī</s> likewise. (89)'

body.translated_text: Again the objector says: let it be that they are worthy of worship. But their names are not heard anywhere. To this too, in the <s>Bhaviṣyottara</s> [Purāṇa], in the context of <s>Malla-dvādaśī</s>, <s>Śrī Kṛṣṇa</s> [speaks] to <s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s>:

body.text: gopālīyaṃ nūnaṃ pādmokta-gāyatrī-carī bhavet | pāliketi saṃjñāyāṃ kaṇa | daśamī tatheti daśamīty api - (end page 27) nāmaikaṃ tac cānvartham iti sarvānte paṭhitam | yad vā tatheti-daśamy api tārakā-nāmnīty arthaḥ | tathā skānde prahlāda-saṃhitāyāṃ dvārakā-māhātmye māyāvasaraḥ prastāve uddhava-gamane (12.25-33) lakṣito vācety ādinā lalitā śyāmalā dhanyā viśākhā rādhā śaivyā padmā bhadrā ity etāni aṣṭau gaṇitāni |
body.translated_text: This <s>Gopālī</s> must indeed be the one who practices the <s>Gāyatrī</s> mentioned in the <s>Padma</s> [Purāṇa]. '<s>Pālikā</s>' [is analyzed] with the suffix <s>kaṇ</s> in the sense of a proper name. '<s>Daśamī</s> likewise' — '<s>Daśamī</s>' is also (end page 27) one name, and it is a significant name [i.e., meaningful] — thus all [names are significant]...

body.text: atha vanitā-śata-koṭibhir ākulitam ity āgama-prasiddheḥ | vanitā-śata-yūthapa iti śrī-bhagavat-prasiddheḥ | anyāny api loka-śāstrayor avagantavyāni |
body.translated_text: Now, because of the well-known statement in the <s>Āgamas</s> — 'accompanied by hundreds of <s>koṭīs</s> of women' — and because of the famous epithet of the Blessed Lord — 'leader of hundreds of groups of women' — other [names] too should be understood from both popular and scriptural [sources].

body.text: atha śata-koṭitvānyathānupapattyā tāsāṃ tan-mahā-śaktitvam eva gamyate | tatrāpi sarvathā śreṣṭhe rādhā-candrāvalīty ubhe | bhaviṣyottare somābhā-śabdena candrāvaly eva sūcitā artha-sāmya-prāyāt | yataḥ śrī-rādhayā saha pratiyogitvam aitihyam asyātra virājate |
body.translated_text: Now, because the number of hundreds of <s>koṭīs</s> cannot be explained otherwise, their status as his great <s>śaktis</s> (powers) is understood. Even among them, 'in every way the most excellent are these two: <s>Rādhā</s> and <s>Candrāvalī</s>.' In the <s>Bhaviṣyottara</s>, by the word '<s>Somābhā</s>' (Moon-radiant), <s>Candrāvalī</s> is indicated, because of the approximate equivalence of meaning...

body.text: tathā ca śrī-bilvamaṅgala-caraṇāḥ -
body.translated_text: And thus, the venerable <s>Bilvamaṅgala</s> [says]:

children.translated_text: Having come from the abode of <s>Rādhā-mohana</s>, [<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>] addressed <s>Candrāvalī</s>:

children.text: rādhe kṣemamayeti tasya vacanaṃ śrutvāha candrāvalī |
children.translated_text: '<s>Rādhe</s>! Is all well?' — hearing his words, <s>Candrāvalī</s> said:

children.text: kaṃsa kṣemamaye vimugdha-hṛdaye kaṃsaḥ kva dṛṣṭas tvayā
children.translated_text: '<s>Kaṃsa</s>! Is all well?' — 'O bewildered one, where did you see <s>Kaṃsa</s>?'

children.text: rādhā kveti vilajjito nata-mukha-smero hariḥ pātu vaḥ ||90||
children.translated_text: 'And where is <s>Rādhā</s>?' — embarrassed, with face bowed and a smile — may that <s>Hari</s> protect you! (90)

body.text: *NOTE: This is a well-known verse, but is not in any of the Bilvamangala collections.
body.translated_text: *NOTE: This is a well-known verse, but is not in any of the <s>Bilvamaṅgala</s> collections.

children.text: tayor apy ubhayor madhye rādhikā sarvathādhikā |
children.translated_text: And of those two, <s>Rādhikā</s> is in every way superior;
She whose very nature is <s>Mahābhāva</s> (Great Ecstatic Love), supremely weighty in her qualities. (91)

body.text: yathoktaṃ matsya-purāṇe dakṣaṃ prati devī-vacanam -
body.translated_text: As stated in the <s>Matsya Purāṇa</s>, the words of the <s>Devī</s> to <s>Dakṣa</s>:

body.text:
rukmiṇī dvāravatyāṃ tu rādhā vṛndāvane vane |
citra-kūṭe tathā sītā vindhye vindhya-nivāsinī |
devakī mathurāyāṃ ca pātāle parameśvarī || ity ādi | (end page 28)

atra rukmiṇī-saha-pāṭhād itthaṃ bodhayati yathā dvārakāyāṃ tasyā eva sarvathādhikyaṃ tathā śrī-vṛndāvane tasyā iti | svarūpa-śakti-vyūha-rukmiṇī-rādhā-devakīnāṃ māyāṃśa-rūpeṇābheda-kathanaṃ tu śaktitva-sādhāraṇyenaiva | yathā jīvātma-paramātmanoś cit-sāmyenaikyaṃ tadvad iti |
body.translated_text: Here, by being listed alongside <s>Rukmiṇī</s>, it is conveyed: just as she [<s>Rukmiṇī</s>] has complete supremacy in <s>Dvārakā</s>, so she [<s>Rādhā</s>] has supremacy in <s>Śrī Vṛndāvana</s>. The statement of non-difference [among] <s>Rukmiṇī</s>, <s>Rādhā</s>, and <s>Devakī</s> — who are manifestations of the <s>svarūpa-śakti</s> — in the form of the <s>Māyā</s>-portion, is due to their [shared] status as <s>śakti</s>...

body.text: atha yathā rukmiṇī-kṛṣṇayoḥ paraspara-śobhitvaṃ śrī-śukena varṇitam - asyaiva bhāryā bhavitum ity ādināṃ [BhP 10.53.37] tathaiva rādhā-kṛṣṇayor api ṛk-pariśiṣṭe śrutyā varṇitam rādhayā mādhavo devo mādhavenaiva rādhikā vibhrājante janeṣv ā iti | vibhrājante vibhrājate ā samyak iti śruti-padārthaḥ | darśitaṃ ca tasyāḥ svarūpaṃ bṛhad-gautamīye baladevaṃ prati śrī-kṛṣṇena -
body.translated_text: Now, just as the mutual adornment of <s>Rukmiṇī</s> and <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> was described by <s>Śrī Śuka</s> — 'she was to become his wife' and so on (<s>Bhāgavata Purāṇa</s> 10.53.37) — so too, the [mutual adornment] of <s>Rādhā</s> and <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> has been described by <s>Śruti</s> in the <s>Ṛk-pariśiṣṭa</s> (supplement to the <s>Ṛgveda</s>): '<s>Mādhava</s> the Lord, with <s>Rādhā</s>...'

children.text: sattvaṃ tattvaṃ paratvaṃ ca tattva-trayam ahaṃ kila |
children.translated_text: Reality, truth, supremacy — I am indeed this triple principle;
She too, <s>Rādhikā</s>, my beloved, embodies the triple principle. (93)
I am beyond <s>Prakṛti</s>; she too is of the nature of my <s>śakti</s>;

children.text: sāttvikaṃ rūpam āsthāya pūrṇo 'haṃ brahma cit-paraḥ ||94||
children.translated_text: Assuming the <s>sāttvika</s> (pure) form, I am the complete <s>Brahman</s>, supreme in consciousness. (94)

body.text:
brahmaṇā prārthitaḥ samyak sambhavāmi yuge yuge |
tvayā sārdhaṃ tayā sārdhaṃ nāśāya devatādruhām ||95|| iti |
body.translated_text:
Petitioned duly by <s>Brahmā</s>, I take birth age after age,
together with you, together with her, for the destruction of those hostile to the gods. (95) — thus.

body.text: atra sattvaṃ kāryatvaṃ tattvaṃ kāraṇatvaṃ paratvaṃ tato 'pi śraiṣṭhyaṃ yat tattva-trayaṃ tad aham ity arthaḥ tathaiva bodhayati tathaivāgre dhyāna-prasaṅge -
body.translated_text: Here: <s>sattva</s> means being an effect; <s>tattva</s> means being a cause; <s>paratva</s> means supremacy beyond even that — the triple principle that I am — this is the meaning. In the same way it conveys [this meaning]; likewise, further, in the context of meditation:

body.text:
devasyābheda-rūpeṇa tapta-hema-sama-prabhām |
rakta-vastra-parīdhānāṃ raktālaṅkāra-bhūṣitām ||96|| (end page 29)

children.translated_text: One should worship <s>Śrī Rādhā</s> on the left side, devoted to <s>bhakti</s>;
The <s>Devī</s> is declared to consist of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>; <s>Rādhikā</s> is the supreme deity. (97)

body.translated_text:
[One should meditate upon her] as non-different from the Lord in form, of a radiance equal to molten gold,
clad in red garments, adorned with red ornaments. (96) (end page 29)

children.translated_text: She should be meditated upon as granting boons and fearlessness, served by all deities;
She who embodies all <s>Lakṣmīs</s>, all radiance, the supreme enchantress. (98)

body.text: atra pūjayed iti kaṇṭhoktir eva | evam agre 'pi mṛtyu-sañjaya-tantre -
body.translated_text: Here, 'one should worship' (<s>pūjayet</s>) is an explicit directive. Likewise, further, in the <s>Mṛtyu-sañjaya Tantra</s>:

body.text:
pīta-vastra-parīdhānāṃ vaṃśa-yukta-karāmbujām |
kaustubhoddīpta-hṛdayāṃ vanamālā-vibhūṣitām |
śrīmat-kṛṣṇāṅghri-palyaka-nilayāṃ parameśvarīm ||99|| ity ādi |
body.translated_text:
'Clad in yellow garments, with a lotus-hand holding a flute,
with a heart illumined by the <s>Kaustubha</s> gem, adorned with a forest garland,
the supreme goddess whose abode is the foot-stool of <s>Śrīmat Kṛṣṇa</s>.' (99) — and so on.

body.text: yathā -
body.translated_text: As follows:

body.text:
sarva-lakṣmī-mayīṃ devīṃ paramānanda-nanditām |
rāsotsava-priyāṃ rādhāṃ kṛṣṇānanda-svarūpiṇīm |
bhaje cidamṛtākāra-pūrṇānanda-mahodadhim ||100|| iti |
body.translated_text: I worship <s>Rādhā</s>, the <s>Devī</s> who embodies all forms of <s>Lakṣmī</s>, who is delighted with supreme bliss, who is dear to the <s>rāsa</s> festival, who is the embodiment of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>'s bliss — an ocean of perfect bliss in the form of conscious nectar. (Verse 100)

body.text: dhyātvety-ādi-sammohana-tantre - cintayed rādhikāṃ devīṃ gopa-gokula-saṅkulām ity ādi ca | asyāḥ śreṣṭhatvam ādi-vārāhe kaṭira-parivartanyāṃ govardhana-parikrame tat-kuṇḍa-prasaṅge yathā -
body.translated_text: 'Having meditated' etc. — in the <s>Sammohana Tantra</s>: 'One should meditate upon <s>Rādhikā Devī</s>, surrounded by the cowherd community and cows,' and so on. Her supremacy [is stated] in the <s>Ādi-Varāha</s>, in the section on the circumambulation of <s>Govardhana</s> in the <s>Kaṭira-parivartanī</s>, in the passage concerning her <s>kuṇḍa</s> (sacred pond), as follows —

children.translated_text: Going north of the <s>Gaṅgā</s>, [to the place] of the God of gods, the wielder of the disc,

children.text: ariṣṭena samaṃ tatra mahad yuddhaṃ pravartitam ||101||
children.translated_text: A great battle was waged there with <s>Ariṣṭa</s>. (Verse 101)
Having slain there <s>Ariṣṭa</s>, who was in the form of a bull,
In anger, by the strike of His heel, a great <s>tīrtha</s> (sacred bathing place) was created. (Verse 102)

children.text: snātas tatra tadā hṛṣṭo vṛṣaṃ hatvā sa-gopakaḥ |
children.translated_text: Having bathed there, joyful after slaying the bull, together with the cowherds,

children.text: vipā mā (?) rādhikāṃ prāha kathaṃ bhadre bhaviṣyati ||103||
children.translated_text: [He] said to <s>Rādhikā</s>: 'How, O blessed one, shall it be?' (Verse 103)

body.text:
tatra rādhā samāśliṣya kṛṣṇam akliṣṭa-kāriṇam |
sva-nāmnā viditaṃ kuṇḍaṃ kṛtaṃ tīrtham adūrataḥ ||104|| (end page 30)

children.translated_text: Known as <s>Rādhā-kuṇḍa</s>, it is auspicious and destroys all sins.
O slayer of <s>Ariṣṭa</s>, by bathing in <s>Rādhā-kuṇḍa</s>, one obtains the fruit

body.translated_text: Then <s>Rādhā</s>, embracing <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> the performer of effortless deeds, created nearby a <s>kuṇḍa</s> (pond) known by her own name as a <s>tīrtha</s> (sacred place). (Verse 104) (end of page 30)

body.text:
rājasūyāśvamedhābhyāṃ nātra kāryā vicāraṇā |
go-hatyā-brahma-hatyādi pāpaṃ kṣipraṃ praṇaśyati ||106|| iti |
body.translated_text: Of the <s>Rājasūya</s> and <s>Aśvamedha</s> [sacrifices] — there should be no doubt about this. Sins such as cow-killing and <s>brāhmaṇa</s>-killing are quickly destroyed. (Verse 106)

body.text: atra satīṣv api sarvāsu tāsu asyā eva tena saha tādṛśa-prema-vyavahāreṇotkarṣāvagamāt śreṣṭhatvam āyātam | tathā vrata-ratnākara-dhṛta-bhaviṣya-purāṇe ca -
body.translated_text: Here, although all of them [the <s>gopīs</s>] are virtuous, her supremacy is established because of the recognition of her preeminence through such an exchange of <s>prema</s> (divine love) with Him. And likewise in the <s>Bhaviṣya Purāṇa</s> as cited in the <s>Vrata-ratnākara</s> —

children.text: bālye 'pi bhagavān kṛṣṇas taruṇaṃ rūpam āśritaḥ |
children.translated_text: Even in childhood, Lord <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> assumed a youthful form

children.text: reme vihārair vividhaiḥ priyayā saha rādhayā ||
children.translated_text: And sported with various pastimes together with His beloved <s>Rādhā</s>.

body.text:
ekadā kārttike māsi paurṇamāsyāṃ mahotsavaḥ |
āsīn nanda-gṛhe ity ādau
body.translated_text: Once, in the month of <s>Kārttika</s>, on the full moon night, there was a great festival in the house of <s>Nanda</s> — thus beginning,

children.text: tasmin dine ca bhagavān rātrau rādhā-gṛhaṃ yayau |
children.translated_text: On that day, the Lord went to <s>Rādhā</s>'s house at night.

children.text: sā ca kruddhā tam udare kāñcī-dāmnā babandha ha ||108||
children.translated_text: And she, being angry, bound Him around the waist with a girdle-cord. (Verse 108)
<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, having told [her] everything about the great festival at His own home,

children.text: priyāṃ prasādayāmāsa tataḥ sā tam avocayat ||109||
children.translated_text: Pleased His beloved; then she said to Him: (Verse 109)

children.text: idaṃ covāca tāḥ kṛṣṇaḥ preyasī prīta-mānasaḥ |
children.translated_text: And <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, His heart delighted, said this to His beloved:

children.text: kāñcī-dāma tvayā tanvi udare yan mayārpitam ||110||
children.translated_text: 'O slender one, this girdle-cord that was placed by you on My waist — (Verse 110)

children.text: dāmodareti me nāma priyaṃ tena śubhānane |
children.translated_text: Because of that, the name <s>Dāmodara</s> (one bound at the waist) is dear to Me, O fair-faced one.

children.text: nātaḥ prītikaraṃ nāma mama lokeṣu vidyate ||111||
children.translated_text: There is no name more pleasing to Me than this in all the worlds. (Verse 111)
On this <s>Prajāpatyā</s> [full moon] day, all <s>siddhis</s> (perfections) will be attained forever.

children.text: bhaktiṃ ca durlabhāṃ prāpya mama loke mahīyate ||112||
children.translated_text: Having obtained the rare <s>bhakti</s> (devotion), one is glorified in My world. (Verse 112)

body.text: ulūkhale yadā mātrā baddho 'haṃ bhavitā priye | (end page 31)
body.translated_text: When, O beloved, I shall be bound with ropes at the waist to a mortar by My mother, (end of page 31)

body.text: udare dāmabhir loke tadā vyaktaṃ bhaviṣyati ||113||
body.translated_text: Then it will become manifest in the world through [ropes at] the waist. (Verse 113)

body.text:
anena nāma-mantreṇa yo 'smin māsi tvayā saha |
mām arcayed vidhānena sa labhet sarva-vāñchitam ||114|| iti |
body.translated_text: By this name-<s>mantra</s>, whoever in this month worships Me together with you according to the prescribed rules shall obtain all desires.' (Verse 114)

body.text: atrāpi priyayā saha rādhayā iti śrī-kṛṣṇecchayā śrī-kṛṣṇavad bālye 'pi āviṣkṛta-nava-yauvanam eva iti jñeyam |
body.translated_text: Here also, 'together with His beloved <s>Rādhā</s>' — by <s>Śrī Kṛṣṇa</s>'s will, it should be understood that, just as <s>Śrī Kṛṣṇa</s>, even in childhood, manifested fresh youthfulness.

body.text:
tata ārabhya nandasya vrajaḥ sarva-samṛddhimān |
harer nivāsātma-guṇai ramākrīḍam abhūn nṛpa ||115|| (BhP 10.5.18)
body.translated_text: 'From then on, the <s>Vraja</s> of <s>Nanda</s>, possessed of all prosperity, became the playground of <s>Ramā</s> (<s>Lakṣmī</s>) through the qualities of <s>Hari</s>'s residence, O King.' (Verse 115) (<s>BhP</s> 10.5.18)

body.text: ity anena śrī-kṛṣṇa-prādurbhāvānantaraṃ tasām āvirbhāva-kathanāt | tatrāpi śrṣṭhatvaṃ pūrvavaj jñeyam | tatra tādṛśa-bhāvair varṇanaṃ tasyāḥ śrī-śukadevenāpi kṛtam |
body.translated_text: By this [verse], because it narrates their manifestation immediately after <s>Śrī Kṛṣṇa</s>'s appearance, her supremacy there too should be understood as before. There, the description of her with such emotional states was also made by <s>Śrī Śukadeva</s> [himself].

body.text:
ekā bhrū-kuṭim ābaddhya prema-saṃrambha-vihvalā |
ghnatīvaikṣat kaṭākṣepaiḥ sandaṣṭa-daśana-cchadā ||116|| (BhP 10.32.6)
body.translated_text: 'One [<s>gopī</s>], having knit her brows, overwhelmed with passionate love, as if striking with sidelong glances, biting her lip—' (Verse 116) (<s>BhP</s> 10.32.6)

body.text: ity anena ekāmukhyā eke mukhyāny akevalā ity amaraḥ | evaṃ śrīmad-gopāla-tapanyāṃ yad gāndharvīti viśrutā sā tu saiva jñeyā | tasyā evaṃ mukhyatvā̆di-liṅgena sarvatra cāvagamāt | ataiva śrī-rādhā-saṃvalita-dāmodara-pūjā kārttike vihitā | śrī-kṛṣṇa-satyabhāmā-saṃvādīye kārttika-māhātmye ca prātaḥ-snāna-saṅkalpa-mantraṃ -
body.translated_text: By [the word] 'one' (<s>ekā</s>) — '<s>eka</s>' means 'chief,' '<s>eka</s>' means 'not ordinary' — according to the <s>Amarakośa</s>. Similarly, in the <s>Śrīmad Gopāla-tāpanī</s>, she who is known as <s>Gāndharvī</s> should be understood as that very same [<s>Rādhā</s>]. Because her primacy is recognized everywhere through such distinguishing marks. For this very reason, the worship of <s>Dāmodara</s> together with <s>Śrī Rādhā</s> is prescribed in <s>Kārttika</s>. And in the <s>Kārttika-māhātmya</s> in the dialogue of <s>Śrī Kṛṣṇa</s> and <s>Satyabhāmā</s>, the <s>saṅkalpa</s>-<s>mantra</s> (intention-formula) for the morning bath —

body.text:
kārttike 'haṃ kariṣyāmi prātaḥ-snānaṃ janārdana |
prīty-arthaṃ tava deveśa dāmodara mayā saha ||117|| [HBV 16.172] [*NOTE: Alternative numbering 16. 84]
body.translated_text: 'In <s>Kārttika</s>, I shall perform the morning bath, O <s>Janārdana</s>, for Your pleasure, O Lord of the gods, O <s>Dāmodara</s>, together with me.' (Verse 117) [<s>HBV</s> 16.172] [NOTE: Alternative numbering 16.84]

body.text: atra mā-sabda-prayogaḥ | tasyāḥ parama-lakṣmī-rūpatvāt | (end page 32)
body.translated_text: Here the use of the word '<s>mā</s>' [refers to <s>Rādhā</s>]. Because she is of the form of the supreme <s>Lakṣmī</s>. (End of page 32)

body.text: arghya-dāna-mantre ca sākṣāt tan-nāmokteḥ | yathā -
body.translated_text: And in the <s>arghya</s>-offering <s>mantra</s>, because her name is directly mentioned. As follows —

children.text: vratinaḥ kārttike māsi snānasya vidhivan mama |
children.translated_text: 'Of the one observing the vow, in the month of <s>Kārttika</s>, for my ritual bath according to the prescribed rules,
O <s>Dāmodara</s>, accept this <s>arghya</s> (offering), O destroyer of the lord of demons. (Verse 118)

body.text:
nitye naimittike kṛtsne kārttike pāpa-śoṣaṇe |
gṛhānārghyaṃ mayā dattaṃ rādhayā sahito hare ||119|| [HBV 16.174-175]
body.translated_text: In the perpetual and occasional [rites] of the entire <s>Kārttika</s> that destroys sins, accept this <s>arghya</s> offered by me, O <s>Hari</s>, together with <s>Rādhā</s>.' (Verse 119) [<s>HBV</s> 16.174-175]

body.text: iti yugmatvena upādānāt tasyā eva śreṣṭhatvam | tad-yugalopāsanāyāṃ bhaviṣya-purāṇa-vacanaṃ darśitam eva | tathā daśādhyāyi-kārttika-māhātmyaṃ cen nūnaṃ pādmānugataṃ syāt tarhi tatra tad-yugalo pāsanaṃ prakaṭataram eveti | tathā vāsanā-bhāṣyotthāpita āgneya-vacane 'pi tasyāḥ śreṣṭhatvam | yathā -
body.translated_text: Because she is taken together [with the Lord] as a couple, her supremacy alone [is established]. The statement of the <s>Bhaviṣya Purāṇa</s> regarding the worship of that couple has already been shown. Furthermore, if the <s>Kārttika-māhātmya</s> in the Ten Chapters follows the <s>Padma</s> [Purāṇa], then the worship of that couple therein is even more manifest. Likewise, in the <s>Āgneya</s> (Agni Purāṇa) passage cited in the <s>Vāsanā-bhāṣya</s>, her supremacy [is established]. As follows —

body.text:
gopyaḥ papracchur uṣasi kṛṣṇānucaram uddhavam |
hari-līlā-vihārāṃś ca tatraikāṃ rādhikāṃ vinā |
rādhā tad-bhāva-saṃlīnā vāsanāyā virāmitā ||120|| ity ādi |
atra tad-bhāva-saṃlīnā ity anena divyonmāda-maya-vacanaṃ madhupa kitava-bandho ity ādikaṃ tasyā eveti vijñāpya sarvāsu gopīṣu tasyāḥ śreṣṭhyaṃ darśitam | yuktaṃ ca tat tu yataḥ | śrī-kṛṣṇānveṣakartrīṇāṃ tāsāṃ tām evoddhiśya tad idaṃ vacanaṃ śrūyate yathā -
body.translated_text: The <s>gopīs</s> asked <s>Uddhava</s>, <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>'s companion, at dawn about <s>Hari</s>'s pastimes and sports — [all] except one, <s>Rādhikā</s>. <s>Rādhā</s>, absorbed in His emotional state, was stopped by the <s>vāsanā</s> (deep impression). (Verse 120) And so on. Here, by 'absorbed in His emotional state,' it is indicated that the speech of divine ecstasy beginning with 'O honey-bee, O deceitful friend' belongs to her alone, and thereby her supremacy among all the <s>gopīs</s> is shown. And this is fitting, because the following statement is heard, addressed to her specifically, by those [<s>gopīs</s>] who were searching for <s>Śrī Kṛṣṇa</s> —

body.text:
anayārādhito nūnaṃ bhagavān harir īśvaraḥ
yan no vihāya govindaḥ prīto 'yam anayad rahaḥ ||121|| (BhP 10.30.28)
apy eṇapatny upagataḥ priyayeha gātrais
tanvan dṛśāṃ sakhi sunirvṛtim acyuto vaḥ |
kāntāṅga-saṅga-kuca-kuṅkuma-rañjitāyāḥ
kundasrajaḥ kulapater iha vāti gandhaḥ ||122|| (BhP 10.30.11)
body.translated_text: 'Surely this one has worshipped the Blessed Lord <s>Hari</s>, the Supreme Controller, for <s>Govinda</s>, having left us, pleased, has taken her away in secret.' (Verse 121) (<s>BhP</s> 10.30.28) 'O friend, has <s>Acyuta</s>, accompanied by His beloved, come here among the deer, extending with His limbs the complete delight of your eyes? Here wafts the fragrance of the garland of <s>kunda</s> flowers of the chief of the clan, colored with the <s>kuṅkuma</s> from the breasts of His beloved whose body is in contact with His.' (Verse 122) (<s>BhP</s> 10.30.11)

body.text: (end page 33)
body.translated_text: (End of page 33)

body.text:
bāhuṃ priyāṃsa upadhāya gṛhītapadmo
rāmānujas tulasikālikulair madāndhaiḥ
anvīyamāna iha vas taravaḥ praṇāmaṃ

children.translated_text: O trees, do you welcome Him as He passes by, with glances of love? (<s>BhP</s> 10.30.12)

body.translated_text: Placing His arm on the shoulder of His beloved, holding a lotus, the younger brother of <s>Rāma</s>, followed by intoxicated bees from the <s>tulasī</s> garland —

body.text: kiṃ bahunā asyāḥ saubhāgya-vāñchā dvārakā-mahiṣīṇām api śrūyate | tatas tāsāṃ tādṛśa-vacanaṃ śrī-śukadevenāpy uditaṃ - yathā na vayaṃ sādhvi sāmrājyam ity ādy uktvā āhuḥ ----
body.translated_text: In brief, the longing for her good fortune is heard even from the queens of <s>Dvārakā</s>. Therefore, such a statement of theirs is also uttered by <s>Śrī Śukadeva</s> — as, after saying 'O virtuous one, we [do not desire] sovereignty,' etc., they said —

children.translated_text: 'We desire to bear on our heads the dust from the blessed feet of <s>Śrī</s> (Fortune) —
Rich with the fragrance of the <s>kuṅkuma</s> from the breasts — [the dust] of the wielder of the mace. (Verse 124)

body.text:
vraja-striyo yad vāñchanti pulindās tṛṇa-vīrudhaḥ |
gāvaś cārayato gopāḥ pāda-sparśaṃ mahātmanaḥ ||125|| iti | [BhP 10.83.42-43]
body.translated_text: The women of <s>Vraja</s>, the <s>Pulindas</s>, the grasses and herbs, the cows, and the cowherds who graze them — [all desire] the touch of the feet of the great-souled one.' (Verse 125) [<s>BhP</s> 10.83.42-43]

body.text: vraja-stry-ādīnāṃ vāñchā darśitā -
body.translated_text: The longing of the women of <s>Vraja</s> and others is shown —

body.text:
pūrṇāḥ pulindya urugāyapadābjarāga-
śrīkuṅkumena dayitāstanamaṇḍitena |
taddarśanasmararujas tṛṇarūṣitena
limpantya ānanakuceṣu juhus tadādhim ||126|| (BhP 10.21.17) ity anena |
body.translated_text: 'The <s>Pulinda</s> women, fulfilled, anointing their faces and breasts with the <s>kuṅkuma</s> of the widely-praised one's lotus feet — the <s>kuṅkuma</s> that adorned His beloved's breasts, that destroyed the pain of lovesickness aroused by His sight, and that was deposited on the grass — they cast off their grief.' (Verse 126) (<s>BhP</s> 10.21.17)

body.text: atra saty urugāya-padābja-rāgety anena (10.21.17) saha dayitā-stana-maṇḍitena ity uktyā tat kuṅkumaṃ dayitā-stanatas tasya pade lagnam iti gamyate | sā ca dayitā kuca-kuṅkuma-gandhyāḍhyam (end page 34) ity eka-vacanānta-nirdeśenānūditā |
body.translated_text: Here, truly, by [the phrase] 'the <s>kuṅkuma</s> from the lotus feet of the widely-praised one' (<s>BhP</s> 10.21.17), together with the expression 'adorned [from] the breasts of His beloved,' it is understood that the <s>kuṅkuma</s> from the beloved's breasts clung to His feet. And that beloved is referred to (end of page 34) by the singular designation 'the <s>kuṅkuma</s> rich with the fragrance of the breasts.'

body.text:
tad idaṃ varṇayantīṣu tāsv api sā viśiṣṭety avagamyate | ayaṃ bhāvaḥ śrītve prasiddhāyāḥ śriyas tatra kāmanaiva śrūyate | na tu saṅgatiḥ | yad vāñchayā śrīr lalanācarat tapo vihāya kāmān suciraṃ dhṛta-vratā iti [BhP 10.16.36] nāgapatnīnām | yā vai śriyārcitam ajādibhir āpta-kāmair ity ādi [BhP 10.47.62] uddhavasyāpi vākyāt | na ca rukmiṇītve prasiddhāyāḥ śriyas tatra saṅgatiḥ | kāla-deśayor anyatamatvāt | na ca vraja-strīṇāṃ śrī-sambandha-lālasā yuktā - nāyaṃ śriyo 'ṅga ity ādinā (10.47.60) tato 'pi paramādhikya-śravaṇāt | tasmād rukmiṇī dvāravatyāṃ tu rādhā vṛndāvane vane ity ādy ukta-siddhāntānusāreṇa sarvato vilakṣaṇā yā śrīr virājate tām uddiśyaiva vraja-devīnāṃ tad idaṃ vākyam | tataś ca tāsāṃ yathā tatra spṛhāspadatā tathāsmākaṃ paṭṭa-mahiṣīṇām
iti | saṅgamaś cāyaṃ divasa eveti sambhāvyate | tatraiva pulindānāṃ bhramaṇāt kuṅkumānāṃ lepana-karmaṇārdratvāvagamāc ca | dvayoḥ saṅgamaś cāyaṃ na sambhoga-viśeṣa-rūpaḥ | rāsa-prasaṅge --
body.translated_text: While they were describing this, it is understood that she [<s>Rādhā</s>] is even among them the most distinguished. The purport is: for the well-known <s>Śrī</s> (Fortune-goddess) who is famous as <s>Lakṣmī</s>, only [her] desire for that place is heard — but not [actual] union. As stated: 'With the desire for which, <s>Śrī</s>, having abandoned [all] desires and observing vows for a long time, practiced austerities as a woman' (<s>Bhāgavatapurāṇa</s> 10.16.36) — [these are] the words of the serpent-wives. And from <s>Uddhava</s>'s own statement: 'That place which <s>Śrī</s> — though worshiped by <s>Brahmā</s> and others whose desires are fulfilled — [aspired to]' and so on (<s>Bhāgavatapurāṇa</s> 10.47.62). Nor is there union there for the well-known <s>Śrī</s> in the form of <s>Rukmiṇī</s>, because of the difference in either time or place. Nor is it fitting for the women of <s>Vraja</s> to yearn for connection with <s>Śrī</s> — since they hear of [<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>'s] supremacy even beyond her, in 'He is not [the property] of <s>Śrī</s>, O friend' and so on (<s>Bhāgavatapurāṇa</s> 10.47.60). Therefore, in accordance with the established conclusion stated as '<s>Rukmiṇī</s> in <s>Dvāravatī</s>, <s>Rādhā</s> in the forest of <s>Vṛndāvana</s>' — this statement of the ladies of <s>Vraja</s> is directed toward that <s>Śrī</s> who is entirely distinct from all others. And thus, just as she is the object of aspiration there, so [she is] for us, the chief queens. And this union is deemed to have been during the daytime — because of the roaming of the <s>Pulindas</s> in that very [area], and because of the understanding of the freshness of the <s>kuṅkuma</s> (saffron) ointment. And this union of the two was not of the nature of a particular amorous encounter. In the <s>rāsa</s> context:

body.text:
bhagavān api tā rātrīḥ śaradotphullamallikāḥ |
vīkṣya rantuṃ manaścakre ity atraiva (BhP 10.29.1) nava-saṅgamasya pratīyamānatvāt | anyathā tatra parīkṣārthaṃ punas tenopekṣāvacanasyāsaṅgatvāpatteḥ | tad idaṃ veṇu-prakaraṇe bhaṇitatvād veṇu-sambandhenaiva gamyate | urugāya ity anenaiṣa eva saṃsūcitaḥ | tasmād kadācid veṇu-kṛtākarṣāyās tasyā labdha-mūrcchāyā mūrcchāśāntaye sa-kuṅkume svinne vakṣasi sambhramataḥ kevalena śrī-caraṇa-sañjīvanī-pallavena spṛśan gevādyāpi
(end page 35)
body.translated_text: 'The Lord too, seeing those autumn nights with blooming jasmine, set his mind to sport' — in this very [passage] (<s>Bhāgavatapurāṇa</s> 10.29.1), a new [first] union is indicated. Otherwise, his words of apparent dismissal there, intended as a test, would be incongruous.

body.text: vādyāpi samyak saṅkocānapagayamat drutam eva sa tasmān niścakrāmeti budhyate | kāścit parokṣaṃ kṛṣṇasya sva-sakhībhyo 'nvavarṇayann iti uktavān | yās tu tad-anyās tāsām eva pūrṇāḥ pulindyaḥ ity ādi vacanam | tasmāt sādhv evoktam lakṣmīr abhitaḥ stritamā ity ādi | varṇitā ca sā tathaiva śrī-jayadeva-sahacareṇa mahārāja-lakṣmaṇa-sena-mantri-vareṇomāpatidhareṇa yathā --
body.translated_text: Since this has been stated in the flute-section (<s>veṇu-prakaraṇa</s>), it is understood in connection with the flute alone. By [the word] '<s>urugāya</s>' (of great fame), this very [incident] is indicated. Therefore, on one occasion, when she who was drawn by the flute had fainted, he — solely to relieve her swoon — touching [her] with the [mere] life-giving sprout of his sacred feet on her perspiring breast bearing <s>kuṅkuma</s> (saffron), in haste,

children.translated_text: With the movements of one [<s>gopī</s>'s] eyebrow-creeper, with another's opening of eyes, with another's smiles
Radiant as moonlight — while being honored on the way by each in a concealed manner,
Upon the face of <s>Rādhā</s> — graced with the beauty of modesty mixed with broken pride-born contempt —
The anxious, entreating glances of the foe of <s>Kaṃsa</s> alighted — may they be victorious! // 127 //

body.translated_text: NOTE: ...

body.text: śrī-jayadevenāpi rādhām ādhāya hṛdaye tatyāja vraja-sundarīḥ | iti (GG 3.1) | patyur manaḥ kīlitam (GG 12.14) iti ca |
body.translated_text: By <s>Śrī Jayadeva</s> also: 'Having placed <s>Rādhā</s> in his heart, he left the beautiful women of <s>Vraja</s>' (<s>Gītagovinda</s> 3.1). And: 'The husband's mind was transfixed' (<s>Gītagovinda</s> 12.14).

body.text: ataiva --
body.translated_text: For this very reason —

children.translated_text: She who is the supreme, highest power (<s>śakti</s>), of the form of <s>Mahāviṣṇu</s>'s own nature;
Merely through the knowledge of her, [one attains knowledge] of the Supreme Self of all supreme beings.

children.text: muhūrtād eva devasya prāptir bhavati nānyathā |
children.translated_text: In but a moment, the attainment of the Lord becomes possible — not otherwise.
She alone, whose nature is the totality of <s>prema</s> (divine love), the sovereign of <s>Gokula</s> —

body.text: anayā sulabho jñeya ādidevo 'khileśvaraḥ ||
body.translated_text: Through her, the primeval Lord, the master of all, is to be known as easily accessible.

body.text: ity utthāpita-pañcarātra-vacanaṃ sarvopari virājamānaṃ bhavatīty alam ativistareṇa pramāṇa-vacana-saṅgraheṇa |
body.translated_text: This statement from the <s>Pañcarātra</s> thus recovered reigns supreme over all — enough with excessive elaboration of the collection of authoritative statements.

children.translated_text: Therefore, among all the <s>gopīs</s>, <s>Rādhikā</s> is the most weighty;
She who is described with all-surpassing [qualities] in the <s>Purāṇas</s>, <s>Āgamas</s>, and other [scriptures]. //

body.text: (end page 36)
body.translated_text: (end of page 36)

body.text: ataḥ sādhūktaṃ śrīdāmodara-rādhārcanam arhati vraja-sthānām ity ādi |
body.translated_text: Therefore it is well said: '<s>Śrī Dāmodara</s> and <s>Rādhā</s> deserve worship among those dwelling in <s>Vraja</s>' — and so on.

children.text: rādhā vṛndāvane yadvat tadvad dāmodaro hariḥ |
children.translated_text: Just as <s>Rādhā</s> in <s>Vṛndāvana</s>, so <s>Dāmodara Hari</s> [in <s>Vṛndāvana</s>];

children.text: darśiteṣu ca śāstreṣu tad-yugmaṃ tat tad-īśituḥ ||
children.translated_text: And in the revealed scriptures, that pair is [described as belonging to] that very Lord. //
The Lord <s>Mādhava</s> with <s>Rādhā</s>, and <s>Rādhikā</s> with <s>Mādhava</s> alone —
They shine among the people — thus says the supplementary text (<s>pariśiṣṭa</s>). //

children.text: na viṣṇunā vinā devī na hariḥ padmajāṃ vinā |
children.translated_text: 'The <s>Devī</s> [does not exist] without <s>Viṣṇu</s>, nor <s>Hari</s> without the lotus-born [<s>Lakṣmī</s>]' —
The <s>Hayagrīva Pañcarātra</s> is here made manifest, because of which //
In the observance of the <s>Kārttika</s> vow, therefore, these paired deities,
Called <s>Rādhā</s>-<s>Dāmodara</s>, are seen in both popular [tradition] and scripture. //

children.text: kiṃ bahūktyā kuṇḍa-yugmaṃ tayor yugmena vīkṣyate |
children.translated_text: What need of many words? The pair of <s>kuṇḍas</s> (sacred ponds) is seen as belonging to that pair;

children.text: śāstre ca darśitā tasmāt kaimutyād yugmatā tayoḥ ||
children.translated_text: And in scripture [their pairing] has been shown — therefore, all the more so, the pairing of those two. //
Some [worship] <s>Umā</s> and <s>Maheśvara</s>; others, <s>Lakṣmī</s> and <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>;

children.text: te bhajantāṃ bhajāmas tu rādhā-dāmodarau vayam ||
children.translated_text: Let them worship [those]; as for us, we worship <s>Rādhā</s> and <s>Dāmodara</s>. //

body.text: iti śrī-vṛndāvana-vāsinaḥ kasyacij jīvasya śrī-rādhā-kṛṣṇārcana-dīpikā sadā dedīpyamānatām apadyatām || śrī-guru-caraṇa-kamalebhyo namaḥ | śrī-kṛṣṇa-caitanya-candrāya namaḥ | śrī-rādhā-dāmodarābhyāṃ namaḥ Padyāvalī 259; SKM 1.55.3, RKAD 260umāpatidharasya ||
body.translated_text: Thus, the <s>Śrī Rādhā-Kṛṣṇārcana-dīpikā</s> (Lamp for the Worship of <s>Śrī Rādhā</s> and <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>) of a certain <s>Jīva</s>, a resident of <s>Śrī Vṛndāvana</s>, may it always shine forth resplendently! Homage to the lotus-feet of the <s>Śrī Guru</s>! Homage to <s>Śrī Kṛṣṇa Caitanya Candra</s>! Homage to <s>Śrī Rādhā-Dāmodara</s>! [Verse of <s>Umāpatidhara</s>: <s>Padyāvalī</s> 259; SKM 1.55.3, RKAD 260.]
